classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: boron_density
items.description: Elemental boron number density, summed over neutral atoms and all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+.
items.documentation:
Boron density is the elemental boron particle density, with neutral boron and every ionic charge state included in one additive quantity.

$$
n_B = \sum_{Z=0}^{5} n_{B,Z}
$$

where $n_B$ is the elemental boron density, $Z$ is the boron ionic charge state with $Z=0$ denoting neutral boron, and $n_{B,Z}$ is the density of boron in state $Z$.

The quantity is the underlying boron density field; [line-averaged boron density](name:line_averaged_boron_density) and [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density) are distinct averages of it. It excludes no boron charge state but is not a charge-state-specific or charge-weighted density.

items.name: plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part
items.description: Plasma mass density imaginary part is the imaginary quadrature of a complex plasma mass-density quantity. It is the component multiplying the positive imaginary basis, not the complete complex density.
items.documentation:
Plasma mass density imaginary part is the imaginary quadrature of a complex plasma mass-density quantity. It represents the coefficient of the imaginary basis in a complex representation of plasma mass density, not the complete complex density itself.

The complex plasma mass density may be decomposed into real and imaginary quadratures as

$$
\rho = \rho_{\mathrm{re}} + i\,\rho_{\mathrm{im}}
$$

where $\rho$ is the complex plasma mass density, $\rho_{\mathrm{re}}$ is its real quadrature, $\rho_{\mathrm{im}}$ is the plasma mass density imaginary part, and $i^2=-1$.

This parent quantity covers imaginary-part plasma mass-density fields independent of the particular origin of the complex representation. The [perturbed plasma mass density imaginary part](name:perturbed_plasma_mass_density_imaginary_part) is a first-order perturbation case. It excludes the real quadrature, the complex modulus, the phase, and the complete complex plasma mass density.

Sign convention: Positive when the quadrature coefficient is along the $+i$ direction in the complex representation of plasma mass density.

items.name: toroidal_plasma_momentum_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Signed total linear momentum along increasing toroidal angle within a closed flux surface as it approaches the magnetic axis, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total toroidal linear momentum carried by electrons and all ion species within the volume enclosed by a closed magnetic flux surface as that surface approaches the magnetic axis. It is a linear-momentum projection, not toroidal angular momentum.

$$
P_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}} = \lim_{\psi\to\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}} \int_{V(\psi)} \sum_s m_s n_s v_{s,\phi}\,dV
$$

Here $P_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the limiting toroidal momentum, $\psi$ is a flux-surface label, $\psi_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is its magnetic-axis value, $V(\psi)$ is the enclosed volume, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, $v_{s,\phi}$ is its toroidal velocity component, and $dV$ is the volume element. The sum includes electrons and ions and excludes neutral species. Its aggregation and projection match [toroidal total plasma momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum), while the corresponding boundary quantity is toroidal total plasma momentum at plasma boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the net enclosed momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized radial diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its local temperature gradient.
items.documentation:
The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient in the radial direction quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in one specified charge state. It is the radial directional specialization of the [ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), applying to the component along increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation for the density-normalized radial diffusive energy flux of charge state $z$ is:

$$
\frac{Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff},R}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E,R}\,\frac{\partial T_{i,z}}{\partial R}
$$

where $Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff},R}$ is the radial component of the diffusive thermal energy flux carried by ions in charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is their number density, $T_{i,z}$ is their [temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature), and $D_{i,z,E,R}$ is this radial diffusion coefficient. The minus sign denotes radial transport down the local radial temperature gradient.

This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not an aggregation over charge states. It excludes convective, advective, and $E \times B$ contributions to the total ion heat flux; the charge-state-aggregated [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is a density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states. Other directional specializations include the [parallel ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and the [poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: power_of_soft_xray_detector
items.description: Band-integrated radiant power received by a soft X-ray detector channel over its selected photon-energy band or bands.
items.documentation:
Soft X-ray detector power is the radiant power carried by incident soft X-ray photons and received by one detector channel after spectral selection. It represents radiation power rather than the detector’s electrical output.

For a selected photon-energy band, the received power is defined by:

$$
P_{\mathcal{B}} = \int_{\mathcal{B}} E\,\Phi_E(E)\,dE
$$

where $P_{\mathcal{B}}$ is the received power for band $\mathcal{B}$, $E$ is photon energy, $\Phi_E(E)$ is the photon arrival-rate density as a function of photon energy, $\mathcal{B}$ is the selected energy interval, and $dE$ is an infinitesimal photon-energy interval.

The quantity applies to soft X-ray radiation received by a particular detector channel and is integrated over photon energy within its selected bandpass. It is not summed over detector channels, viewing directions, or distinct energy bands; when multiple bands are resolved, each band has its own band-integrated received-power value. It excludes plasma-emitted power before arrival at the detector and electrical power generated by detector electronics.

The quantity is distinct from [spectral_efficiency_of_soft_xray_detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_soft_xray_detector), which describes the probability of registering an incident photon rather than the received radiant power. It is also distinct from [hard_xray_brightness](name:hard_xray_brightness), which describes photon radiance rather than the power collected by a channel over its energy band and collection geometry.

items.name: neutral_density
items.description: Neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms and molecules in the unresolved neutral population. Unless a resolved variant is specified, it aggregates over neutral species, thermal and suprathermal populations, internal quantum states, and parent-ion-associated neutral states.
items.documentation:
Neutral density is the local number density of electrically neutral atoms and molecules in the unresolved neutral population. It is a pointwise volumetric particle density, not a flux-surface-averaged or volume-averaged quantity unless an averaging operation is part of the named quantity.

The local aggregate neutral density is defined by the neutral particle count per volume element:

$$
n_0 = \frac{dN_0}{dV} = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathcal{P}_0} n_\alpha
$$

where $N_0$ is the number of neutral particles in the infinitesimal volume element $dV$, $\mathcal{P}_0$ is the set of neutral population classes included by the unresolved quantity, and $n_\alpha$ is the local density of population class $\alpha$.

For the unresolved name, $\mathcal{P}_0$ includes neutral species, thermal and suprathermal kinetic populations, internal quantum states, and parent-ion-associated neutral states that are not otherwise resolved by the standard name. When only thermal and fast kinetic classes are distinguished, the aggregate satisfies $n_0 = n_{0,\mathrm{thermal}} + n_{0,\mathrm{fast}}$, corresponding to [thermal_neutral_density](name:thermal_neutral_density) and [fast_neutral_density](name:fast_neutral_density). It excludes ions, electrons, and any averaging represented by [volume_averaged_density](name:volume_averaged_neutral_species_density).

items.name: y_direction_unit_vector_of_camera
items.description: Signed direction cosine giving a camera’s pointing direction along the y axis of the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The camera direction-vector component along the y axis is the signed direction cosine of its pointing direction in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis. It specifies the projection of the camera viewing direction onto the Cartesian y axis.

The component is defined by

$$
d_y = \hat{\mathbf{d}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}}
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{d}}$ is the camera pointing-direction unit vector and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the positive y-axis unit vector. Its value forms part of the normalized direction vector together with the [x-axis camera direction component](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_camera) and [z-axis camera direction component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera), satisfying $d_x^2+d_y^2+d_z^2=1$.

This quantity describes camera pointing direction, not image-up orientation; that distinct orientation is represented by the [camera y image-up unit-vector component](name:y_image_up_unit_vector_of_camera).

items.name: co_passing_power_density
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric energy source rate for the co-passing orbit population, representing energy transfer to or from particles circulating in the co-current direction.
items.documentation:
Co-passing power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which kinetic energy is transferred to or from the co-passing orbit population per unit physical volume. Co-passing particles are passing particles that circulate continuously in the co-current direction.

For a flux surface labeled by poloidal magnetic flux $psi$, it is defined as

$$
p_{E,\mathrm{co}}(\psi)=\left\langle\frac{dE_{\mathrm{co}}}{dt\,dV}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the kinetic energy of the co-passing population, $t$ is time, $V$ is physical volume, and the angle brackets denote a flux-surface average. Positive values denote net energy gain by this population; negative values denote net energy loss. Wave-particle interactions, collisions, and particle sources may contribute. The related [counter-passing power density](name:counter_passing_power_density) applies the same energy-transfer definition to the oppositely circulating orbit class, while power density is the unqualified parent quantity.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_boron_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description: Dimensionless global boron abundance ratio using separately volume-averaged boron and electron number densities, with neutral boron and every ionic charge state included.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the global abundance of elemental boron relative to the electron population. It characterizes plasma composition over the full plasma volume rather than at a local point or along a line of sight.

The defining ratio is

$$
f_B = \frac{\overline{n}_B}{\overline{n}_e}
$$

where $f_B$ is the boron-to-electron abundance ratio, $\overline{n}_B$ is the volume-averaged elemental boron number density, and $\overline{n}_e$ is the volume-averaged electron number density. The overbar denotes averaging over the plasma volume.

The numerator includes neutral boron and every ionic boron charge state, while the denominator represents the complete electron population. For the associated plasma-composition convention, the ratio is evaluated at the time of peak electron density.

This quantity is distinct from local [boron density](name:boron_density) and from [line-averaged boron density](name:line_averaged_boron_density): it is a quotient of two separately volume-averaged densities, not a volume average of a pointwise ratio or a line average. Its numerator is the [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density), making this ratio the corresponding normalized composition measure.

items.name: incident_angle_at_wall
items.description: Incident angle at wall is the angle between the incoming neutral-particle velocity and the wall-surface normal directed into the material. It is the species-specific angular coordinate for physical sputtering by neutral projectiles; zero is normal incidence and grazing incidence approaches a right angle.
items.documentation:
Incident angle at wall is the geometrical angle between the velocity direction of an incident neutral particle at impact and the local wall-surface normal directed from the plasma-facing side into the wall material. It characterizes the incidence direction of a selected neutral-particle species on the wall.

The incidence angle $\alpha$ is defined by

$$
\alpha = \arccos\left(\hat{\mathbf{v}}_\mathrm{inc}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{in}\right)
$$

where $\hat{\mathbf{v}}_\mathrm{inc}$ is the unit direction of the incoming neutral-particle velocity at the impact point and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_\mathrm{in}$ is the local wall-surface unit normal directed into the wall material.

The scope is a specified neutral incident species interacting with the wall. The allowed interval is $0 \le \alpha \le \pi/2$: $\alpha=0$ corresponds to normal incidence into the wall, and $\alpha=\pi/2$ corresponds to tangential grazing incidence. Directions for which the particle is leaving the wall-facing half-space are not incident angles.

This quantity is the angular argument for the physical sputtering dependence of that neutral species at the wall. It is not the physical sputtering coefficient, not an angle for emitted or sputtered particles, and not an average over neutral species or wall locations.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_polarizer
items.description: Major-radius coordinate of the polarizer’s geometric reference point, namely its circular center or local-plane origin, measured from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the major-radius location of a polarizer’s geometric reference point. This point is the center for a circular polarizer or the origin of the local coordinate system describing a planar polarizer.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the coordinate is defined from the point’s horizontal Cartesian coordinates by

$$
R_{\mathrm{pol}} = \sqrt{x_{\mathrm{pol}}^2+y_{\mathrm{pol}}^2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the polarizer reference point’s major-radius coordinate, and $x_{\mathrm{pol}}$ and $y_{\mathrm{pol}}$ are its horizontal coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis. Here $R$ denotes major radius, $\phi$ denotes toroidal angle, and $Z$ denotes vertical height.

The quantity applies only to the polarizer reference point and is nonnegative; it is not the radial coordinate of an arbitrary point on the polarizer surface and is not a flux-surface-normal projection. It is the polarizer-specific realization of the general [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate).

Together with the [toroidal coordinate of the polarizer](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_polarizer), this coordinate locates the same geometric reference point in the cylindrical frame.

items.name: accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative post-breakdown carbon inventory from gas injection, expressed as six equivalent-electron counts for every injected neutral carbon atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of carbon atoms delivered by gas injection, represented as an equivalent-electron count. It excludes carbon introduced during the plasma prefill phase and does not represent an instantaneous source rate or a charge-state-resolved ion inventory.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}(t)=6N_{\mathrm{C}}(t)=6\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}^{\mathrm{gas}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{C,eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the cumulative number of injected carbon atoms, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C}}^{\mathrm{gas}}$ is the carbon injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation time. The factor 6 is carbon's atomic number. This is the post-breakdown component of carbon count due to gas injection and is distinct from [carbon prefill count due to gas injection](name:carbon_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: neutral_species_particle_diffusivity
items.description: Effective Fickian transport coefficient relating neutral-species particle flux to neutral-species number-density gradients, with directional components represented by more specific quantities.
items.documentation:
Neutral-species particle diffusivity is the effective transport coefficient for particle spreading driven by a neutral-species number-density gradient. It is the neutral-species specialization of [particle diffusivity](name:particle_diffusivity), with directional components represented by more specific quantities.

For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive particle flux of neutral species $s$ is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{n},s,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{\mathrm{n},s,i}\,\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{n},s}}{\partial x_i}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{n},s,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle flux of neutral species $s$ along direction $i$, $D_{\mathrm{n},s,i}$ is the corresponding neutral-species particle diffusivity component, $n_{\mathrm{n},s}$ is the number density of neutral species $s$, and $x_i$ is the coordinate along the resolved transport direction. The minus sign defines down-gradient diffusive transport for a positive coefficient.

This quantity selects the neutral-species population but does not select a transport direction, neutral state, or microscopic mechanism. Direction-specific instances include [parallel neutral-species particle diffusivity](name:parallel_neutral_species_particle_diffusivity). When a neutral species is decomposed into neutral states, the species-level diffusivity is the density-weighted mean over those states; the state-resolved counterpart is [neutral-state particle diffusivity](name:neutral_state_particle_diffusivity).

items.name: net_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating
items.description: Net ion-cyclotron heating power is the radio-frequency energy absorbed per unit time by the plasma from a specific launcher, excluding losses outside the plasma.
items.documentation:
Net ion-cyclotron heating power is the rate at which radio-frequency waves from a specific launcher transfer energy to the plasma. It includes absorption by all plasma particle populations, not only ions.

The absorbed power is defined by

$$
P = \int_{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} p_{\mathrm{abs}}\,dV
$$

where $P$ is the net absorbed power attributable to the launcher, $V_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the entire plasma volume, $p_{\mathrm{abs}}$ is the local radio-frequency energy-transfer rate per volume summed over all absorbing plasma populations and averaged over a radio-frequency cycle, and $dV$ is a volume element.

This quantity applies to one launcher, not a sum over launchers. Unabsorbed wave power and dissipation outside the plasma are excluded.

The [launched power of an ion-cyclotron heating antenna](name:launched_power_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is the forward-minus-reflected power directed into the vessel before plasma absorption; it need not equal the absorbed power defined here. The [total power due to ion-cyclotron heating](name:total_power_due_to_ion_cyclotron_heating) sums launched power over all heating antennas and therefore differs in both absorption scope and launcher aggregation.

items.name: parallel_co_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged stress along the magnetic field carried by suprathermal particles whose untrapped orbits follow the plasma-current direction, including directed motion.
items.documentation:
The parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure is the field-aligned kinetic stress of suprathermal particles, averaged over a magnetic flux surface. Co-passing particles occupy untrapped guiding-center orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion follows the plasma current.

In the nonrelativistic kinetic description, this component is defined by the parallel second velocity moment:

$$
p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}(S) = \left\langle m_s \int v_\parallel^2 f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_S
$$

where $p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged parallel co-passing fast-particle pressure of species $s$, $S$ is the magnetic flux surface, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_S$ denotes its volume-weighted thin-shell average. Here $m_s$ is the particle mass, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing suprathermal portion of the species distribution function, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The parallel velocity is $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{b}$, where $\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$.

This quantity applies to the fast population of the represented species, not a total over all fast-ion species. Multiple fast-particle distribution contributions for that species add linearly. The velocity moment is not centered on the population's mean velocity, so directed parallel motion contributes. Thermal particles, trapped particles, counter-passing particles, and transverse stress are excluded.

It is the co-passing orbit-class contribution to the [parallel fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure). Its relationship to the [co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) is $\langle p_s^{\mathrm{co,fast}}\rangle_S=(p_{\parallel,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}+2p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}})/3$, where $p_s^{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the local kinetic trace pressure and $p_{\perp,s}^{\mathrm{co,fast}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged transverse stress per perpendicular degree of freedom for the same species and orbit class. Thus the parallel component is not the isotropic trace pressure.

items.name: current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Electric-current-density contribution driven by plasma pressure gradients, including the perpendicular diamagnetic current and its associated field-aligned return current.
items.documentation:
Current density due to diamagnetic drift is the pressure-gradient-driven contribution to [electric current density](name:current_density) in a magnetized plasma. It includes the perpendicular diamagnetic drive and the associated field-aligned return current, rather than denoting a projection onto a diamagnetic direction.

In the isotropic-pressure fluid limit, its decomposition is

$$
\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}=\frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}+j_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}}\hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic-drift current-density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $p$ is the total isotropic pressure of the charged plasma populations, and $\nabla p$ is its spatial gradient. The magnetic-field unit vector is $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$, and $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the [parallel current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), defined by $j_{\parallel,\mathrm{dia}}=\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

The contribution is summed over charged plasma populations and is not restricted to a particular species or to the plasma edge. It is mechanism-resolved: projecting the total current from all mechanisms onto a diamagnetic direction does not isolate this contribution. Independently driven currents are excluded.

Under stationary quasineutral current closure, the associated field-aligned return current balances the divergence of the perpendicular diamagnetic drive. The [Pfirsch–Schlüter current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:pfirsch_schlueter_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) identifies the specific return-current contribution associated with toroidal magnetic geometry; it is not the entire current-density vector.

Sign convention: Positive when a projected component represents net positive-charge transport along its defining positive direction; the parallel projection is positive along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$.

items.name: vertical_neutral_velocity
items.description: Mean directed motion of a selected neutral species along the vertical symmetry-axis direction, averaged over contributing internal states with number-density weighting.
items.documentation:
The vertical neutral velocity is the projection of the bulk drift of a selected neutral species onto the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. It represents directed motion after averaging over particle velocities and contributing internal states.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position, its local definition is:

$$
u_{0,Z}=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_0=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\mathbf v\,f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{0,Z}$ is the vertical neutral velocity, $\mathbf u_0$ is the [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) vector, $\hat{\mathbf z}$ is the unit vector along the vertical symmetry axis, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, $f_{0,a}$ is the local velocity distribution of neutral internal state $a$, and $\mathcal A$ is the set of contributing internal states. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The state distributions combine with number-density weighting for one selected neutral species, not by summing state velocities or averaging different species together. This is a local flow component, including for neutrals in the scrape-off layer and divertor, rather than a spatial average, flow-speed magnitude, particle flux, or random thermal spread.

Unlike [bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), which retains one specified internal state, this quantity averages over the contributing internal states before taking the vertical projection.

Sign convention: Positive when the neutral bulk flow points toward increasing vertical position $Z$.

items.name: total_counter_passing_particle_pressure
items.description: Total pressure of counter-passing particles is the flux-surface average of one-third of their kinetic-stress trace, including thermal, nonthermal, and directed-motion contributions.
items.documentation:
Total pressure of counter-passing particles is the flux-surface-averaged isotropic part of the kinetic stress carried by the thermal and nonthermal populations of a specified species. Counter-passing particles occupy untrapped guiding-center orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma current.

The nonrelativistic kinetic definition is

$$
p_{s,\mathrm{cp}} = \left\langle \frac{m_s}{3}\int_{\mathrm{cp}} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $p_{s,\mathrm{cp}}$ is the total counter-passing pressure of species $s$, $m_s$ is its particle mass, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the [particle distribution](name:particle_distribution) including its thermal and nonthermal parts, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integration domain $\mathrm{cp}$ selects counter-passing orbits, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a magnetic-flux-surface average weighted by the differential volume between neighboring surfaces. Velocity is not centered on the counter-passing population's mean flow, so directed-motion stress is retained.

“Total” denotes the additive thermal and nonthermal contributions within the specified species, not a sum over all plasma species. Contributions from multiple distributions representing that species are superposed. Trapped and co-passing particles are excluded. This quantity is a flux-surface average rather than a local pressure at a point on the surface; it combines all three velocity degrees of freedom without assuming isotropy and is not a single field-parallel or field-perpendicular stress component.

The [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure) restricts the kinetic moment to suprathermal particles, whereas this quantity also includes the thermal contribution. The [total co-passing particle pressure](name:total_co_passing_particle_pressure) applies the thermal-plus-nonthermal scope to the opposite passing-orbit class.

items.name: current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
items.description: Net toroidal plasma current generated non-inductively by wave–particle interactions, including cumulative and toroidal-mode-resolved representations.
items.documentation:
Wave-driven current is the toroidal plasma current attributable to momentum transfer from externally applied electromagnetic waves through wave–particle interactions. It excludes inductive current and non-wave non-inductive current sources.

For a selected poloidal cross-sectional area, the current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{wd}} = \int_A j_{\mathrm{wd},\phi}(R,Z)\,dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{wd}}$ is the wave-driven current, $A$ is the selected poloidal area, $j_{\mathrm{wd},\phi}$ is the toroidal component of the wave-driven current density, and $(R,\phi,Z)$ is the right-handed cylindrical frame. For a flux-surface-enclosed area, this gives the cumulative quantity represented by [toroidal current due to wave-driven current drive](name:toroidal_current_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive); the same current may be decomposed into per-toroidal-mode current.

Sign convention: Positive when the wave-driven plasma current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: ion_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed cylindrical-R flux density of toroidal linear momentum for the ion population, attributed to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
items.documentation:
Ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed cylindrical-$R$ flux density of toroidal linear momentum carried by the ion population and associated with its pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift. The transported momentum is the $\hat{\phi}$ component and the flux direction is $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counterclockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The diamagnetic contribution is defined by summing the charge-state contributions to the toroidal momentum flux:

$$
\Pi_{R\phi,i}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \sum_{\alpha} m_i n_{i,\alpha} u_{\phi,i,\alpha} v_{R,i,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $\Pi_{R\phi,i}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this momentum flux, $\alpha$ labels the included charge states, $m_i$ is the ion mass, $n_{i,\alpha}$ is the charge-state number density, $u_{\phi,i,\alpha}$ is its toroidal flow velocity, and $v_{R,i,\alpha}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is its cylindrical-$R$ diamagnetic-drift velocity.

This quantity is the ion-population specialization of [momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) and is charge-state aggregated, whereas [ion charge state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) retains one charge state. It excludes momentum-flux contributions from non-diamagnetic transport mechanisms.

Sign convention: Positive when positive toroidal linear momentum is transported toward increasing $R$.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_line_of_sight
items.description: Major-radius coordinate of the second reference point on a line of sight, equal to its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of line of sight

The coordinate is defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal coordinates of the second reference point in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, with $z$ the vertical coordinate and the $z$ axis coinciding with the toroidal symmetry axis.

The coordinate is nonnegative and vanishes on the toroidal symmetry axis. It is distinct from a distance along the line of sight, a minor-radius distance measured from the magnetic axis, and a magnetic flux label. Like the [radial coordinate of a measurement position](name:radial_coordinate_of_measurement_position), it locates a specified point; no summation, line integration, averaging, or emission weighting is implied.

items.name: radial_volumetric_force
items.description: Radial component of the electromagnetic body-force density vector, projected onto the direction of increasing major radius R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial volumetric force is the $\hat{R}$-projection of the local electromagnetic body-force density $\mathbf{f} = \mathbf{J} \times \mathbf{B}$ acting on plasma volumes or conducting wall and structural elements. It characterizes the net radial push or pull arising from the interaction of local current density with the magnetic field, driving stress and displacement in the major-radial direction.

The defining relation is the radial projection of the Lorentz force density in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$:

$$
f_R = (\mathbf{J} \times \mathbf{B}) \cdot \hat{R} = J_\phi B_Z - J_Z B_\phi
$$

where $\mathbf{J}$ is the current density vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $J_\phi$, $J_Z$, $B_\phi$, $B_Z$ are the toroidal and vertical components respectively.

This component is computed in magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium analyzes and disruption-load assessments to quantify radial electromagnetic stresses on plasma-facing components, wall tiles, and blanket structures. Together with [toroidal_volumetric_force](name:toroidal_volumetric_force) and [vertical_volumetric_force](name:vertical_volumetric_force), it resolves the complete local electromagnetic body-force density vector described by [volumetric_force](name:volumetric_force).

Sign convention: Positive when the electromagnetic force points in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: ion_torque_density
items.description: Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume for all ion species and charge states, retaining the complete torque-vector direction.
items.documentation:
Torque density for all ion species and charge states is the net angular-momentum transfer rate to the ion population per unit volume. It retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than selecting a toroidal component or a particular transfer mechanism.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{i}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i}$ is the ion torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{L}_{i}$ is the total angular momentum of all ion species and charge states in the volume element $\Delta V$, and $t$ is time.

Unless a mechanism qualifier is present, the quantity is the net sum of all applicable angular-momentum transfer contributions. The parent [torque density](name:torque_density) gives the corresponding general torque-density concept, while [toroidal ion torque density](name:toroidal_ion_torque_density) is its major-radius-weighted toroidal projection.

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along the corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

items.name: resistance_of_vacuum_vessel
items.description: Lumped ohmic opposition to current flow through a discrete passive-conductor element of the vacuum vessel.
items.documentation:
Electrical resistance of a discrete passive-conductor element is the proportionality between the voltage drop across the element and the current through it, representing irreversible ohmic dissipation.

$$
R = \frac{\Delta V}{I}
$$

where $R$ is the resistance, $\Delta V$ is the potential difference across the element, and $I$ is the through-current. For an approximately homogeneous element, resistance is determined by the material resistivity and the element geometry, as described by [resistivity of the vacuum vessel](name:resistivity_of_vacuum_vessel) and [resistivity of wall material](name:resistivity_of_wall_material). This lumped quantity excludes inductive opposition and represents only the ohmic component; it is distinct from the total resistance of a closed [passive loop](name:resistance_of_passive_loop).

items.name: ion_momentum_source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Diamagnetic-drift contribution to the local ion momentum-balance source, summed over ion charge states and resolved for the represented momentum projection.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the diamagnetic-drift contribution to an area-normalized local source in the ion linear-momentum balance. It represents pressure-gradient-driven transport of the represented momentum projection and combines the contributions from all ion charge states, excluding neutral momentum.

$$
S_{i,\ell}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \sum_Z S_{i,Z,\ell}^{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $S_{i,\ell}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the aggregate ion momentum source, $S_{i,Z,\ell}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is its contribution for ionic charge state $Z$, and $\ell$ denotes the represented linear-momentum projection. This is the ion-specific contribution to the generic [momentum source due to diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), distinct from the associated [ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift).

Sign convention: Positive when diamagnetic-drift momentum transfer acts in the positive direction of the represented momentum projection.

items.name: vertical_neutral_momentum_diffusivity
items.description: Vertical neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal vertical component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor, governing down-gradient redistribution of aggregate neutral momentum density along Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. The vertical qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the momentum component.
items.documentation:
Vertical neutral momentum diffusivity is the diagonal vertical component of an effective neutral-particle momentum diffusivity tensor. It parameterizes down-gradient diffusive transport of aggregate neutral momentum density along the $Z$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The vertical qualifier identifies the flux and gradient direction, not the momentum component.

For a diagonal Fick's-law closure, the vertical diffusive flux of a neutral momentum-density component is

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\alpha Z} = -D^{(n)}_{m,Z}\,\frac{\partial P_{n,\alpha}}{\partial Z}
$$

where $\alpha$ labels the transported momentum component, $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}_{n,\alpha Z}$ is the vertical diffusive flux of that momentum component, $D^{(n)}_{m,Z}$ is the vertical neutral momentum diffusivity, $P_{n,\alpha}$ is the aggregate neutral momentum density component, and $Z$ is vertical height. The minus sign denotes down-gradient diffusion: for positive diffusivity, the diffusive flux is directed from larger toward smaller aggregate neutral momentum density along $Z$.

This coefficient applies to the aggregate neutral population represented by the neutral momentum-density field. It does not denote a diffusivity for a particular transported momentum component, and it is distinct from off-diagonal tensor components or convective transport of neutral momentum.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity
items.description: Poloidal component of the complex first-order plasma velocity perturbation eigenfunction in linear MHD stability analysis, projected onto the poloidal direction in the flux-coordinate frame (ρ, θ, φ) for a single toroidal Fourier mode.
items.documentation:
The poloidal perturbed plasma velocity is the $\theta$-directed component of the linearized plasma velocity perturbation eigenfunction $\delta\mathbf{v}(\mathbf{r})$, obtained by projecting the full complex perturbation vector onto the poloidal basis direction in the flux-coordinate frame $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$, where $\rho$ is a radial flux surface label and $\theta$ is the poloidal angle. It characterizes the oscillatory poloidal plasma flow about a magnetohydrostatic equilibrium for a specified toroidal Fourier mode number $n$, encoding both the spatial amplitude and phase variation of that flow component along and across flux surfaces.

The physical perturbation follows the eigenfunction ansatz:

$$
\delta v_\theta(\rho, \theta, \phi, t) = \mathrm{Re}\!\left[\delta\hat{v}_\theta(\rho, \theta)\, e^{i(n\phi - \omega t)}\right]
$$

where $\delta\hat{v}_\theta(\rho, \theta)$ is the complex poloidal amplitude profile, $n$ is the toroidal mode number, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $\omega$ is the complex MHD eigenfrequency whose imaginary part gives the mode growth or damping rate.

The complex amplitude decomposes into its [real part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part) and [imaginary part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part), which together specify the amplitude and spatial phase of the poloidal velocity oscillation at each point on a flux surface. Alongside the [radial component](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part) and the [toroidal component](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part), the poloidal projection completes the velocity eigenfunction and supports incompressibility assessment and MHD energy partition calculations in linear stability solvers.

Sign convention: Positive when the poloidal velocity is directed in the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in the flux-coordinate frame $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$.

items.name: ethylene_prefill_count
items.description: Ethylene prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethylene (C2H4) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 16 equivalent electrons per molecule.
items.documentation:
Ethylene prefill count is the total amount of neutral ethylene (C2H4) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral ethylene molecule contributes sixteen equivalent electrons: twelve from two carbon atoms and four from four hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = (2Z_{\mathrm{C}}+4Z_{\mathrm{H}})N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = 16N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}16\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{C}}=6$ and $Z_{\mathrm{H}}=1$ are the atomic numbers of carbon and hydrogen, $N_{\mathrm{C_2H_4,prefill}}$ is the accumulated ethylene-molecule count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_4}}$ is the ethylene introduction rate, and $t_0$ and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ are the prefill start and plasma-breakdown times.

This quantity includes only neutral ethylene introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the ethylene component of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count); [accumulated_ethylene_count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count) represents the distinct post-breakdown accumulation, while [ethane_prefill_count](name:ethane_prefill_count) applies the same convention to a different molecule.

items.name: volume_averaged_electron_temperature
items.description: Temperature of bulk electrons from random translational motion, volume-averaged inside the last closed magnetic flux surface, including during plasma initiation.
items.documentation:
Temperature of bulk electrons averaged over the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface is the spatial mean of their local energy-equivalent kinetic temperature. For nonrelativistic electrons, the local temperature equals two-thirds of the mean random kinetic energy per particle, excluding directed mean-flow energy.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\langle T_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V T_e\,dV
$$

where $\langle T_e\rangle_V$ is the volume-averaged electron temperature, $T_e$ is the local bulk electron temperature, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $dV$ is the differential physical-volume element.

The quantity applies throughout that enclosed volume, including during plasma initiation. Its aggregation convention is an arithmetic spatial volume average, not a density-weighted particle average or a local value. It differs from [line-averaged electron temperature](name:line_averaged_electron_temperature), which averages along a plasma chord. It is neither total electron thermal energy nor a radiation brightness temperature.

This quantity is obtained by applying volume averaging to [electron temperature](name:electron_temperature); [volume-averaged ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_ion_temperature) applies the corresponding spatial average to a specified ion species. It supplies the denominator of the [ratio of magnetic-axis to volume-averaged electron temperature](name:ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature), which expresses central electron-temperature peaking relative to the plasma-wide mean.

items.name: radius_of_detector
items.description: Radius from the center to the circumferential edge of a detector's circular front face, defining its geometric size for optical throughput.
items.documentation:
The detector radius is the geometric distance from the center of a circular detector front face to its circumferential edge.

The corresponding circular face area is defined by

$$
A_{\rm det} = \pi r_{\rm det}^{2}
$$

where $A_{\rm det}$ is the detector front-face area, $r_{\rm det}$ is the detector radius, and $\pi$ is the mathematical constant.

This quantity applies only when the detector front face has circular geometry. It describes the detector face itself and does not represent a collimating aperture, a filter opening, or a width parameter for a noncircular detector geometry.

The face area determined by this radius contributes to the geometric optical throughput represented by [spectrometer etendue](name:etendue_of_spectrometer); it is distinct from the radius of a separate [spectrometer aperture](name:radius_of_aperture).

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Nonnegative factor scaling the collisionless free-streaming cap on the flux of magnetic-field-parallel momentum carried by a specified ion charge state in edge-plasma transport.
items.documentation:
This coefficient scales the collisionless free-streaming bound on transport of the magnetic-field-parallel component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by one specified ion charge state in an edge-plasma fluid closure. Parallel identifies the transported momentum component, not necessarily the direction in which that momentum crosses a surface.

The coefficient enters the flux bound as:

$$
\left|\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{lim}}(\hat{n})\right| \leq \alpha_{s,\parallel}\,\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}(\hat{n})
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $\parallel$ denotes the local magnetic-field direction, $\hat{n}$ is the unit normal to the transport surface, $\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited flux of parallel momentum through that surface, $\Pi_{s,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude, and $\alpha_{s,\parallel}$ is this limiter coefficient. The reference magnitude and the detailed limiting function are closure-dependent.

The coefficient is nonnegative and charge-state resolved; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge states. It scales the flux-magnitude bound without reversing the underlying flux direction and is distinct from a momentum diffusivity or damping rate.

It specializes the [ion charge-state momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) to magnetic-field-parallel momentum. The [diamagnetic momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:diamagnetic_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) instead limits transport of the diamagnetic momentum contribution.

items.name: electron_pressure
items.description: Electron kinetic pressure is one-third of the trace of the velocity-space stress, covering thermal, suprathermal, and combined populations.
items.documentation:
Electron kinetic pressure is the isotropic scalar measure of momentum flux generated by random electron motion about the population mean velocity. It may describe a suprathermal component, a thermal component, or their combined electron population.

The defining pressure is

$$
p_e = \frac{m_e}{3}\int \lvert \mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_e\rvert^2 f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $p_e$ is the electron kinetic pressure, $m_e$ is the electron mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is an individual electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the mean velocity of the represented electron population, $f_e(\mathbf{v})$ is its velocity distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

At parent scope, the quantity applies to a selected thermal or suprathermal electron population or to their full aggregate. Aggregation is over the represented electrons in velocity space, not over ion or neutral species; the full aggregate combines disjoint thermal and suprathermal contributions.

This quantity is the trace-based scalar reduction of the electron kinetic stress and does not specify a directional pressure-tensor component. An anisotropic electron stress is therefore represented here only through its trace, while ion pressure, neutral pressure, and individual tensor components are excluded.

The [fast-electron pressure contribution](name:fast_electron_pressure) is the suprathermal component within this common kinetic-pressure concept. The [total electron pressure](name:total_electron_pressure) is the aggregate over the designated thermal and suprathermal electron populations and equals their sum when those components are disjoint.

items.name: area_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description: Non-negative geometric area of the conducting material within a toroidal-field-coil conductor’s cross-sectional boundary, measured normal to its local centerline.
items.documentation:
The area of a toroidal-field-coil conductor is the geometric area occupied by conducting material in a cross-section normal to the conductor’s local centerline. It excludes any void, bore, insulation, or surrounding aperture.

The area is defined by

$$
A_{\mathrm{cond}} = \iint_{S_{\mathrm{cond}}} dS
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductor cross-sectional area, $S_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the region enclosed by the conductor boundary, and $dS$ is its differential area element.

This quantity complements the conductor dimensions represented by the [width of the toroidal field coil](name:width_of_toroidal_field_coil) and [height of the toroidal field coil](name:height_of_toroidal_field_coil); it is not the area enclosed by a winding or loop.

items.name: neutral_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Neutral state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of linear momentum carried by a specified neutral state and attributed to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift.
items.documentation:
Neutral state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of linear momentum carried by a specified neutral state and associated with its pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic drift. The quantity denotes the diamagnetic contribution without selecting a particular flux direction or transported momentum component.

The contribution is defined componentwise by:

$$
\Pi_{ab,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \rho_{\mathrm{ns}} v_{a,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}} u_{b,\mathrm{ns}}
$$

where $\Pi_{ab,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the momentum flux, $a$ is its flux-direction index, $b$ is its transported-momentum index, $\rho_{\mathrm{ns}}$ is neutral-state mass density, $v_{a,\mathrm{ns}}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic drift velocity, and $u_{b,\mathrm{ns}}$ is neutral-state linear flow velocity.

This is the neutral-state specialization of [momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It excludes contributions attributed to other transport mechanisms and is closely related to [neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux](name:neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_flux).

Sign convention: Positive when the transported neutral-state momentum crosses the oriented reference surface along its positive flux direction.

items.name: first_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description: Full physical extent of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along its first local tangential axis. This object-local axis is tangent to the mirror surface and is the axis parameterized by the first local tangential coordinate; the width applies to rectangular mirror geometry.
items.documentation:
Full physical extent of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror along its first local tangential axis is the edge-to-edge span of the mirror surface in that object-local tangential direction. The first local tangential axis is the axis parameterized by the [first local tangential coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).

For a rectangular mirror surface, let $u_1$ denote the first local tangential coordinate on the mirror surface $\mathcal{M}$. The width is the range of that coordinate over the mirror surface:

$$
w_1 = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{M}} u_1(\mathbf{x}) - \min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathcal{M}} u_1(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $w_1$ is the first local tangential width and $\mathbf{x}$ is a point on the mirror surface.

This quantity applies to rectangular mirror geometry and is distinct from both a coordinate value at a point and the [second local tangential width](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror). As a full extent rather than a signed displacement, it is unchanged by reversing the positive sense of the first local tangential coordinate.

items.name: neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless vector flux-limiter coefficient that scales the free-streaming upper bound on neutral-particle momentum-flux density component-by-component in edge-plasma transport closures.
items.documentation:
The neutral momentum coefficient is the neutral-particle specialization of the general momentum_coefficient vector, providing one dimensionless limiter factor per spatial direction for neutral momentum transport in multi-fluid edge plasma models. Each directional component independently bounds the corresponding neutral momentum flux density, preventing unphysical exceedance of the free-streaming limit when the neutral mean free path is large relative to macroscopic gradient scales.

The component $\alpha_\alpha$ in direction $\hat{e}_\alpha$ is defined as the ratio of the modeled flux to its free-streaming upper bound:

$$
\alpha_\alpha = \frac{\Pi_\alpha}{\Pi_\alpha^{\rm free}}
$$

where $\Pi_\alpha$ is the modeled neutral momentum flux density in direction $\hat{e}_\alpha$ and $\Pi_\alpha^{\rm free} = m_n n_n u_\alpha^{\rm free}$ is the free-streaming estimate, with $m_n$ the neutral particle mass, $n_n$ the neutral number density, and $u_\alpha^{\rm free}$ the direction-$\alpha$ free-streaming reference speed. The constraint $\alpha_\alpha \in [0, 1]$ ensures the closure preserves the sign of the momentum flux while bounding its magnitude. The field-aligned component is analogous to parallel_neutral_state_momentum_coefficient, which resolves the same quantity by internal neutral state.

Components are computed within edge-plasma transport closures as a function of local collisionality; values near 1 characterize the collision-dominated limit, while values near 0 indicate strongly free-streaming conditions where the limiter actively constrains the flux.

items.name: outer_radius_of_passive_loop
items.description: Outer radius of the annular cross-section of a passive conducting loop element is the Euclidean distance from the cross-section center to its outer conducting boundary.
items.documentation:
Outer radius of the annular cross-section of a passive conducting loop element is the Euclidean distance, in the $(R,Z)$ plane at fixed toroidal angle $phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, phi, Z)$ frame, from the center of the annular conductor cross-section to its outer conducting boundary. Here $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The outer boundary radius is defined by the poloidal-plane distance from the cross-section center to the selected outer-boundary point:

$$
r_\mathrm{outer} = \sqrt{(R_\mathrm{outer} - R_c)^2 + (Z_\mathrm{outer} - Z_c)^2}
$$

where $(R_c,Z_c)$ is the annulus-center position and $(R_\mathrm{outer},Z_\mathrm{outer})$ is the outer-boundary position in the same fixed-$\phi$ plane; all coordinate components in the equation are measured in meters.

This quantity is the outer member of the [radius of a passive loop](name:radius_of_passive_loop) family. Together with the [inner radius of a passive loop](name:inner_radius_of_passive_loop), it defines the conducting annulus; for a circular annulus, the cross-sectional area is $A=\pi(r_\mathrm{outer}^2-r_\mathrm{inner}^2)$ and the radial thickness is $r_\mathrm{outer}-r_\mathrm{inner}$. It is nonnegative and is not the loop center's major-radius coordinate or a signed cylindrical component.

items.name: fast_neutron_flux_of_correction_coil
items.description: Incident crossing rate of fast neutrons per unit area on the inboard-facing surface of a non-axisymmetric correction coil.
items.documentation:
Fast neutron number flux is the incident crossing rate of the fast-neutron population per unit area on the inboard-facing surface of a non-axisymmetric correction coil. It is the fast-neutron component of neutron flux of correction coil.

The differential number flux is defined by

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{fast}} = \frac{dN_{\mathrm{fast}}}{dA\,dt}
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the number of fast neutrons incident on surface area $A$ and $t$ is time; $A$ is measured in m$^2$ and $t$ in s.

The inboard-facing surface is the side directed toward decreasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This quantity includes only incident fast-neutron crossings and excludes outgoing crossings and the energy-integrated neutron flux.

items.name: alfven_frequency
items.description: Alfvén frequency at a given radial position for a single toroidal mode number is the complex local shear-Alfvén continuum angular frequency; its real part gives oscillation and its imaginary part gives growth or damping for the stated time dependence.
items.documentation:
Alfvén frequency at a given radial position for a single toroidal mode number is the complex local shear-Alfvén continuum angular frequency for perturbations propagating along the magnetic field on the flux surface at that radial position. Its [real part](name:alfven_frequency_real_part) is the oscillatory component, and its [imaginary part](name:alfven_frequency_imaginary_part) is the temporal growth or damping component.

The ideal shear-Alfvén continuum relation defining the underlying continuum frequency is

$$
\omega_A = |k_\parallel| v_A
$$

where $\omega_A$ is the real continuum angular frequency, $k_\parallel$ is the component of the wave vector parallel to the magnetic field, and $v_A$ is the Alfvén speed, $B/\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_m}$ with $B$ the magnetic-field magnitude, $\mu_0$ the vacuum permeability, and $\rho_m$ the plasma mass density.

This quantity denotes the full complex frequency $\Omega_A=\operatorname{Re}(\Omega_A)+i\operatorname{Im}(\Omega_A)$, not either component alone, and it is an angular frequency rather than a cyclic frequency. The radial position is a flux-surface label in explicitly named flux coordinates such as $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ or $(\psi,\theta,\phi)$, not a cylindrical vector component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. At fixed toroidal mode number, $k_\parallel$ is determined by field-line pitch, magnetic geometry, and poloidal harmonic content, with the [safety factor](name:safety_factor) entering common single-harmonic specializations.

Sign convention: Positive when $\operatorname{Im}(\Omega_A)$ makes perturbations proportional to $\exp(-i\Omega_A t)$ grow exponentially in time.

items.name: thermal_electron_power_density
items.description: Volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy deposition into bulk thermal electrons, including its average over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Thermal-electron power density is the rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to the bulk thermal electron population per unit physical volume. Its flux-surface-averaged form describes the mean deposition on a magnetic flux surface; the underlying local quantity describes deposition within that surface.

The flux-surface-averaged deposition is defined by

$$
\overline{p}_{\mathrm{e,th}} = \left\langle p_{\mathrm{e,th}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}} = \left\langle \frac{dP_{\mathrm{abs,e,th}}}{dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\overline{p}_{\mathrm{e,th}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged thermal-electron power density, $p_{\mathrm{e,th}}$ is the local thermal-electron power density, $P_{\mathrm{abs,e,th}}$ is the coherent-wave power absorbed by thermal electrons within physical volume $V$, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes an average over the magnetic flux surface.

The recipient population is restricted to bulk thermal electrons. Absorption by nonthermal electrons belongs to [fast-electron absorbed wave power density](name:fast_electron_absorbed_wave_power_density). This quantity is the direct wave-absorption contribution to [electron power density](name:electron_power_density), not the net sum of all electron heating and cooling channels; it excludes [collisional electron energy exchange](name:electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), including subsequent collisional redistribution of deposited energy.

[Mode-resolved thermal-electron power density](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_power_density) specializes this deposition by individual toroidal Fourier harmonic. Flux-surface averaging retains the volumetric normalization rather than integrating over the enclosed volume. Integrating that average with the enclosed-volume measure gives the [cumulative thermal-electron absorbed power inside the flux surface](name:thermal_electron_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

items.name: x_coordinate_of_divertor_target
items.description: Signed Cartesian x-coordinate locating the geometric center of a divertor target surface in the right-handed (x, y, z) frame, with +x at toroidal angle φ = 0.
items.documentation:
The x coordinate of a divertor target is the signed Cartesian position of the geometric center of its target surface. It locates that center in the right-handed Cartesian basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$, where $\hat{z}$ is vertical and the positive x direction is horizontal at toroidal angle $\phi=0$.

The coordinate is defined by projection of the center position onto the Cartesian x unit vector:

$$
x_c = \mathbf{r}_c \cdot \hat{\mathbf{x}}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_c$ is the position vector of the target-surface geometric center, $\hat{\mathbf{x}}$ is the Cartesian x unit vector, and $x_c$ is the resulting signed coordinate. The corresponding center location is completed by the [y coordinate of the divertor target](name:y_coordinate_of_divertor_target) and [z coordinate of the divertor target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target); this quantity does not specify the target surface extent.

Sign convention: Positive when the target center lies in the direction of increasing Cartesian x from the coordinate origin.

items.name: propane_prefill_count
items.description: Propane prefill count is the total amount of C3H8 introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 26 count units per neutral propane molecule.
items.documentation:
Propane prefill count is the total amount of neutral propane (C3H8) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each propane molecule contributes 26 equivalent electrons: 18 from three carbon atoms and 8 from eight hydrogen atoms.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating the injected propane molecules over the prefill interval:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = (3Z_C + 8Z_H)N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = 26N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_\mathrm{bd}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8,prefill}}$ is the accumulated propane molecule count, $Z_C=6$ and $Z_H=1$ are the atomic numbers of carbon and hydrogen, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}$ is the propane molecule injection rate, $t_0$ is the start of prefill, and $t_\mathrm{bd}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only propane introduced before breakdown and excludes later fueling, other gas species, and the retained or ionized inventory. It uses the common equivalent-electron bookkeeping of [prefill_count](name:prefill_count), with [ethane_prefill_count](name:ethane_prefill_count) providing the analogous molecular-species convention.

items.name: parallel_total_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective field-parallel advection coefficient for transport of aggregate ion momentum in the edge plasma, distinct from the ion bulk-flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing advective, non-diffusive transport of aggregate ion [momentum](name:momentum) along the local magnetic field in the edge plasma. It is a transport-closure coefficient, not the ion bulk-flow velocity.

For a selected transported momentum component, the convective flux satisfies:

$$
\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} g_i
$$

where $\Pi_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the field-parallel convective flux of that ion momentum component, $V_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection coefficient, and $g_i$ is the corresponding aggregate ion momentum density. The subscript $i$ identifies the ion population. The parallel direction follows $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$, where $\mathbf B$ is the local magnetic field and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is its direction unit vector.

The transported momentum density is summed over the included ion species and their ionic charge states; electron and neutral momentum are excluded. The coefficient acts on this aggregate momentum density and is not a sum of charge-state convection velocities. The parallel qualification specifies the transport direction, not an additional restriction on the transported momentum component.

This quantity is the field-parallel projection of [ion momentum convection velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity). Unlike [total momentum convection velocity](name:total_momentum_convection_velocity), it applies specifically to ion momentum rather than total plasma momentum. It is distinct from [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity): the convective coefficient multiplies momentum density, whereas the diffusive coefficient multiplies its negative gradient.

Sign convention: Positive when effective momentum convection is along the local magnetic-field direction.

items.name: ion_power_due_to_collisions
items.description: Volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred to the total ion population, aggregating both thermal and fast ion sub-populations across all ion species and charge states without prescribing the thermal or fast character of the receiving ions.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the volume-integrated net rate of energy transfer into the complete ion population from Coulomb scattering interactions with all colliding plasma constituents. As a structural abstraction within the collisional-power family, it aggregates thermal and fast ion receiving populations across all ion species and charge states without resolving which ion sub-population receives the energy.

The volume-integrated ion collisional power is defined as:

$$
P_{\rm ion,coll} = \int_V Q_{\rm ion,coll}(\mathbf{r}) \, dV
$$

where $Q_{\rm ion,coll}$ is the local [ion power density due to collisions](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) into the aggregate ion receiving population and the integral extends over the plasma volume $V$.

The receiving population is charge-state-summed for each ion species and species-summed over the ion population. Collisional exchanges among ion sub-populations contained in this aggregate cancel in the all-ion sum; the retained value is the net transfer between the aggregate ion population and populations outside that aggregate, including the complementary electron power due to collisions. Population-resolved components include [fast ion power due to collisions](name:fast_ion_power_due_to_collisions), [thermal ion power due to collisions](name:thermal_ion_power_due_to_collisions), and the charge-state-resolved [ion-state power due to collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_power_due_to_collisions); [power due to collisions](name:power_due_to_collisions) is the corresponding population-abstract parent.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb scattering interactions transfer net energy into the complete ion population.

items.name: thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from fast or non-Maxwellian particles to thermal ions, summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Thermal-ion collisional power density is the signed local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from a designated fast or non-Maxwellian particle population to thermal ions. It is an energy source or sink for the thermal recipient population, not its stored kinetic-energy density.

The exchange is defined by the kinetic-energy moment of the recipient collision operator:

$$
P_{\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{i\in\mathcal{I}}\sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_i|\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{iq,d}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}},f_d](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the thermal-ion collisional power density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is recipient velocity, $\mathcal{I}$ is the included set of thermal-ion species, $i$ labels an ion species, $q$ is its ionic charge number, and $m_i$ is its particle mass. The function $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal recipient distribution for species $i$ and charge state $q$, $f_d$ is the designated donor distribution, and $d$ labels the donor species. The operator $C_{iq,d}$ gives the collisional rate of change of the recipient distribution caused by that donor; the integral covers recipient velocity space.

The quantity is summed over all ionic charge states of each included species, with the species set comprising either one species or several. The [charge-state-resolved thermal-ion collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) supplies an individual species-and-charge-state contribution. Contributions from multiple designated donor distributions add. The quantity is locally defined and is not intrinsically flux-surface averaged; a flux-surface average represents the corresponding average of this local exchange.

This is the thermal-recipient contribution to [ion collisional power density](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), excluding energy deposited into fast-ion or electron recipients. It includes all donor orbit classes. Orbit-restricted quantities, such as [co-passing thermal-ion collisional power density](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions), select the corresponding donor orbits. Summing co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped contributions for the same recipients recovers the unrestricted exchange; applying the same flux-surface average preserves this decomposition.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from the designated donor population to the thermal ions.

items.name: helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron helium-3 source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected helium-3 atom contributes two equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The helium-3 source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral helium-3 is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas-injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Each helium-3 atom contributes two equivalent-electron counts because helium has atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{He}} = 2$.

The defining relation is:

$$
\dot{S}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}} = Z_{\mathrm{He}}\,\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}} = 2\,\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}}$ is the helium-3 equivalent-electron source rate due to gas injection, $\dot{N}_{^{3}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{gas}}$ is the raw neutral helium-3 atomic delivery rate due to gas injection, and $Z_{\mathrm{He}}$ is the atomic number of helium.

This quantity is isotope-specific: it applies only to neutral helium-3 gas admitted through gas injection and is aggregated over all gas-injection paths feeding the plasma vessel. It excludes helium-4 and other injected species, particle sources not due to gas injection, and raw gas-particle accounting represented by the gas particle source rate over vessel due to gas injection.

It is the time derivative of the [accumulated helium-3 count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection) under the same equivalent-electron weighting. Summing species-specific equivalent-electron source rates over active injected species gives the [source rate due to gas injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). The [helium-4 source rate due to gas injection](name:helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) uses the same helium atomic-number weighting but applies to a different isotope, whereas the [hydrogen source rate due to gas injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) differs through the hydrogen atomic number.

Sign convention: Positive when helium-3 gas is delivered into the plasma vessel, increasing the helium-3 equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: total_implicit_ion_particle_source_rate
items.description: Total implicit ion particle source rate is the coefficient multiplying total ion number density in the density-proportional contribution to its particle-number source.
items.documentation:
Total implicit ion particle source rate is the coefficient of the density-proportional, implicit contribution to the total-ion particle-number source. It multiplies total ion number density in the decomposed density transport equation.

The source decomposition is defined by

$$
S_i^{\mathrm{tot}} = S_{i,\mathrm{exp}}^{\mathrm{tot}} + S_{i,\mathrm{imp}}^{\mathrm{tot}} n_i^{\mathrm{tot}}
$$

where $S_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the net total-ion particle source per physical volume, $S_{i,\mathrm{exp}}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is its explicit contribution, $S_{i,\mathrm{imp}}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is this implicit source coefficient, and $n_i^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is total ion number density. The explicit contribution is independent of the density being advanced within this decomposition; the implicit contribution is the coefficient multiplied by that density.

Total ion number density is summed over all included ion species and ionic charge states, counting ions without charge weighting and excluding electrons and neutral particles. The coefficient acts on this aggregate density; it is not itself the full volumetric source or a volume-integrated particle production rate.

This quantity is the total-ion specialization of the [implicit ion particle source rate](name:implicit_ion_particle_source_rate). In contrast, the [implicit ion-state particle source rate](name:implicit_ion_state_particle_source_rate) multiplies the density of a specified ion state rather than the aggregate ion density.

Sign convention: Positive when the density-proportional contribution adds ions to the total ion population; negative values represent removal.

items.name: power_at_divertor_target
items.description: Power at a divertor target is the rate at which energy is deposited on one divertor target by a specified physical deposition channel, integrated over the target's wetted strike-zone surface.
items.documentation:
Power at a divertor target is the rate at which energy is deposited on one divertor target by a specified physical deposition channel, integrated over the target's wetted strike-zone surface. The specified channel denotes a particular physical contribution to deposition and does not by itself imply an all-channel target total.

The deposited power for target $t$ and channel $c$ is defined from the channel-resolved energy-flux-density vector over that surface:

$$
