P_{t,c} = -\int_{A_t} \mathbf{S}_{E,c}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}_t(\mathbf{x}) \, dA
$$

where $P_{t,c}$ is the deposited power on target $t$ due to channel $c$, $A_t$ is the target's wetted strike-zone surface, $\mathbf{S}_{E,c}$ is the energy-flux-density vector for channel $c$, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_t$ is the normalized surface normal directed from the target material toward the plasma-facing side, $\mathbf{x}$ labels a point on the target surface, and $dA$ is the surface element. The leading minus sign makes flux directed from the plasma toward the target material contribute to the deposited target power.

The channel label may distinguish conductive, convective, particle, radiative, or other deposition mechanisms, but this name does not prescribe a decomposition. For a complete mutually exclusive set of channel contributions on the same target, the channel sum equals the surface integral of the total [energy flux at a divertor target](name:energy_flux_at_divertor_target); all-channel target powers at the inner and outer divertor targets are represented by power at inner divertor target and power at outer divertor target. Conductive and convective channel contributions are represented by [power at divertor target due to conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction) and [power at divertor target due to convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection), respectively.

items.name: argon_prefill_count
items.description: Argon prefill count is the total amount of neutral argon (Ar) introduced before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18 per atom.
items.documentation:
Argon prefill count is the total amount of neutral argon (Ar) introduced during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral argon atom contributes 18 equivalent electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating injected argon atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the argon atomic number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} N_{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t)\,dt = 18\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-argon atom count, $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}=18$ is the argon atomic number, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only argon introduced before breakdown and excludes wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and retained or ionized inventory. It is the argon-specific component of [prefill count](name:prefill_count) and follows the isotope-resolved convention used for tritium prefill count.

items.name: accumulated_ethane_count
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of ethane molecules injected after plasma breakdown, assigning 18 equivalent-electron counts to each neutral C2H6 molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the post-breakdown cumulative ethane-gas inventory expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each neutral C2H6 molecule contributes 18 counts: 12 from its two carbon atoms and 6 from its six hydrogen atoms.

The accumulated count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 18\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the ethane molecule injection rate, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, and $t$ is the evaluation time.

This quantity is the accumulated post-breakdown form of the ethane count convention. It excludes ethane introduced during prefill, represented by [ethane prefill count](name:ethane_prefill_count), and differs from the instantaneous [ethane source rate](name:ethane_source_rate).

items.name: field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description: Species-resolved temperature averaged by arc length along an open magnetic field line between upstream and downstream locations in the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the temperature of a specified plasma species averaged along an open magnetic field line traversing the scrape-off layer. It represents the common field-line-averaged quantity instantiated by the electron and ion species-specific children.

The field-line average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{\sigma,\mathrm{FL}} = \frac{\int_{\ell_u}^{\ell_d} T_\sigma(\ell)\,d\ell}{\int_{\ell_u}^{\ell_d} d\ell}
$$

where $\overline{T}_{\sigma,\mathrm{FL}}$ is the field-line-averaged temperature, $\sigma$ identifies the selected plasma species, $T_\sigma(\ell)$ is its local temperature, and $\ell$ is arc length along the open magnetic field line. The limits $\ell_u$ and $\ell_d$ identify the upstream and downstream endpoints of the averaging interval.

The quantity applies to one species at a time and uses an arc-length average along the open field line; it is neither a sum nor an average over multiple species. It is restricted to the scrape-off layer and does not denote a local temperature at one point or a volume average over that region.

This is the field-line-averaged, species-resolved specialization of [average temperature over the scrape-off layer](name:average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer). Its concrete realizations include [electron field-line average temperature over the scrape-off layer](name:electron_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer) and [ion field-line average temperature over the scrape-off layer](name:ion_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer), which differ only by the selected species.

items.name: ion_average_temperature_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Kinetic temperature of the charged-ion population at an internal transport barrier, defined as the arithmetic mean of charged-ion species temperatures, excluding electrons and neutral species.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the arithmetic mean of the kinetic temperatures of all charged ion species on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier. It retains the locus and population scope of average temperature at an internal transport barrier.

$$
T_{i,\mathrm{avg}} = \frac{1}{N_i}\sum_{s\in\mathcal{C}} T_{i,s}
$$

where $\mathcal{C}$ is the set of included charged ion species, $N_i$ is the number of species in that set, and $T_{i,s}$ is the kinetic temperature of species $s$. For each species, $T_{i,s}$ is the density-weighted mean over its charge-state temperatures, using $T_{i,s}=\sum_Z n_{s,Z}T_{s,Z}/\sum_Z n_{s,Z}$, where $n_{s,Z}$ is the number density of charge state $Z$ and $T_{s,Z}$ is its [ion charge-state temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature). Charge-state weighting is therefore applied within each species, but distinct ion species are averaged equally; electrons and neutral species are excluded.

items.name: density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Particle number density of a specified plasma population evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, with charge-state aggregation determined by the population.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local number density of a selected plasma population at the flux-surface location assigned to an internal transport barrier. It applies to electrons, individual ion species, and compound fuel populations treated as effective species.

The number density is defined by

$$
n = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n$ is the number density in m$^{-3}$, $N$ is the number of counted particles, and $V$ is volume in m$^{3}$. For an ion species, the count is summed over its ionic charge states and excludes neutral atoms; electrons are counted directly. The ion density at the internal transport barrier and [electron density at the internal transport barrier](name:electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) are specific population instances, while the [deuterium-tritium density at the internal transport barrier](name:deuterium_tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) treats the fuel mixture as one effective population. The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep density gradients.

items.name: parallel_electric_field_at_separatrix
items.description: Parallel electric field at the separatrix is the electric field projected along the local magnetic field on the separatrix. It fixes the field-aligned projection and separatrix locus, while more specific names may add an aggregation over that locus.
items.documentation:
Parallel electric field at the separatrix is the component of the electric-field vector along the local magnetic-field direction evaluated on the separatrix. The separatrix is the magnetic flux surface that separates the closed-field-line region from the open-field-line edge region.

The field-aligned component at a separatrix point is defined by the projection:

$$
E_\parallel(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{E}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}}(\mathbf{x}), \qquad \mathbf{x}\in S
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is a spatial point on the separatrix $S$, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of the local magnetic-field vector $\mathbf{B}$, and $E_\parallel$ is the resulting parallel electric field.

The scope is limited to the separatrix locus and to the component along $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$; it is not the electric-field magnitude, a component perpendicular to the magnetic-field direction, or a flux-surface-normal projection. This parent quantity does not by itself fix a spatial aggregation over the separatrix; an aggregation qualifier belongs to a more specific quantity.

The [flux-surface averaged parallel electric field at the separatrix](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_electric_field_at_plasma_boundary) is the flux-surface average of this same $E_\parallel$ over $S$; it differs only by specifying the aggregation, while the parallel projection and separatrix evaluation are already part of the present quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric-field vector has a component in the direction of the local magnetic-field vector at the separatrix.

items.name: voltage_of_mass_spectrometer
items.description: Mass-spectrometer detector bias voltage is the signed detector-bias potential difference between the detector electrode or electron-multiplying stage and its bias reference. It is a device-level setting; voltage_of_mass_spectrometer_channel denotes a channel-specific detector bias.
items.documentation:
Mass-spectrometer detector bias voltage is the signed detector-bias potential difference applied between the detector electrode or electron-multiplying stage and its bias reference. It is a device-level electrical setting that affects ion collection efficiency or electron-multiplier gain.

The detector-bias potential difference is defined by the detector and reference electric potentials:

$$
V_\mathrm{bias} = \Phi_\mathrm{det} - \Phi_\mathrm{ref}
$$

where $V_\mathrm{bias}$ is the detector bias voltage of the mass spectrometer, $\Phi_\mathrm{det}$ is the electric potential of the detector electrode or electron-multiplying stage, and $\Phi_\mathrm{ref}$ is the electric potential of its bias reference.

This quantity applies to the mass spectrometer as a device-level detector bias common to the instrument or defined independently of channel selection. It excludes channel-specific detector biases, which are represented by [mass-spectrometer channel detector bias voltage](name:voltage_of_mass_spectrometer_channel).

This quantity is distinct from [mass-spectrometer channel ion current](name:ion_current_of_mass_spectrometer_channel): the ion current is the electrical current associated with collected ions in a channel, whereas the detector bias voltage is the applied potential difference that can affect collection efficiency or gain.

Sign convention: Positive when the detector electrode or electron-multiplying stage is at higher electric potential than its bias reference.

items.name: per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_power_density
items.description: Thermal-electron absorbed wave power density per toroidal mode is the volumetric rate of coherent-wave energy absorption by bulk thermal electrons attributed to an individual toroidal mode number. It is represented locally across a poloidal cross-section or as a flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Thermal-electron absorbed wave power density per toroidal mode is the rate at which coherent-wave energy is absorbed by the bulk thermal-electron population per unit physical volume, attributed to an individual toroidal mode number.

For toroidal mode number $n_\phi$, the local absorbed power density is defined as

$$
p_{e,n_\phi}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{dE^{\mathrm{abs}}_{e,n_\phi}}{dt\,dV}(\mathbf{x})
$$

where $p_{e,n_\phi}$ is the absorbed power density attributed to mode $n_\phi$, $E^{\mathrm{abs}}_{e,n_\phi}$ is the energy absorbed by thermal electrons from coherent waves attributed to that mode, $t$ is time, $V$ is physical volume, $dV$ is a volume element, $\mathbf{x}$ is position in a poloidal cross-section, $n_\phi$ is the toroidal mode number, and $e$ identifies the electron population.

The recipient population is bulk thermal electrons, and the mode index identifies an individual contribution to absorbed wave power. The quantity may describe the local deposition across a poloidal cross-section or its average over a magnetic flux surface. It excludes absorption by fast electrons and ions, as well as electron energy transfer from non-wave processes. The mode-resolved quantity is not a Fourier coefficient of the spatially varying deposition field or a volume-integrated power.

For a complete modal decomposition, summing the contributions over mode numbers gives the mode-summed coherent-wave absorbed power density for bulk thermal electrons. This is one recipient-population component of the [total absorbed wave power density per toroidal mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_total_absorbed_wave_power_density), and contributes to the broader [thermal-electron power density](name:thermal_electron_power_density), which can include non-wave energy transfers. Integrating one mode's density over a physical volume gives the corresponding [thermal-electron absorbed wave power per toroidal mode](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_electron_absorbed_wave_power).

items.name: rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion
items.description: Global volume-integrated rate of fusion events or reaction-product generation attributable to fusion between two nonthermal fuel-ion populations supplied by neutral beams.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the global rate of beam-beam fusion events or of production of a specified reaction product caused by collisions between two nonthermal fuel-ion populations originating from beam injection. It is a reaction-source quantity, not a local source density or directional flux.

The global rate is the volume integral of the local beam-beam fusion source rate:

$$
\dot{N}_X = \int_V S_X^{\mathrm{BB}}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3\mathbf{r}
$$

where $\dot{N}_X$ is the global rate for counted entity $X$, $X$ denotes either a fusion event or a specified reaction product, $V$ is the plasma volume over which beam-beam reactions occur, $S_X^{\mathrm{BB}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the corresponding local source rate density, and $\mathbf{r}$ is position.

The quantity aggregates the volume-integrated contribution from all represented beam-beam fuel-ion reaction channels and, when a product is specified, applies the corresponding product yield. Both reacting fuel-ion populations are nonthermal beam-origin populations; the generic quantity does not select a particular isotope pair, charge state, reaction product, or product channel. It excludes beam-thermal and thermal-thermal fusion contributions, as well as local source densities and surface or directional fluxes.

The [neutron rate due to beam-beam fusion](name:neutron_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion) is a product-specific specialization that counts neutrons while retaining the same global volume integration and beam-beam channel aggregation. The [source rate due to beam-beam fusion](name:source_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion) represents the corresponding product-resolved source-rate family, whereas [rate due to beam-thermal fusion](name:rate_due_to_beam_thermal_fusion) uses one beam-origin and one thermal reacting population and is therefore a distinct fusion mechanism.

items.name: total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous total rate at which neutral gas is introduced into the lower vacuum-vessel region by gas injection valves, summed over lower-region valves and expressed using the equivalent-electron convention across injected species.
items.documentation:
Instantaneous total rate at which neutral gas is introduced into the lower vacuum-vessel region by gas injection valves is the lower-region aggregate equivalent-electron source rate due to gas injection. It counts each injected neutral atom or molecule by the number of electrons associated with its neutral composition and sums over all injected species and all lower-region gas-injection valves.

The multi-species aggregate is defined by:

$$
\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{lower}} = \sum_{v \in \mathrm{lower}} \sum_m E_m\,\dot{N}_{v,m}
$$

where $\dot{N}_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{lower}}$ is this total lower gas source rate, $\dot{N}_{v,m}$ is the neutral gas injection rate of atomic or molecular species $m$ from lower-region valve $v$, and $E_m = \sum_a \nu_{a,m} Z_a$ is the equivalent-electron count for one neutral injected particle of species $m$, with $\nu_{a,m}$ the stoichiometric count of atom $a$ in species $m$ and $Z_a$ its atomic number.

This quantity is an injected source into the vacuum vessel and excludes pumping, wall recycling, ionization losses after entry, and gas introduced outside the lower region. Species-level quantities such as [neon source rate](name:neon_source_rate) and [propane source rate](name:propane_source_rate) are individual species contributions under the same equivalent-electron convention; gas source rate of the vacuum vessel due to gas injection is the vessel-level source quantity without the lower-region restriction.

Sign convention: Positive when neutral gas is introduced into the vacuum vessel through lower-region injection valves.

items.name: counter_passing_power_density
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric energy source rate for counter-passing particles, representing energy transfer to or from particles circulating opposite to the plasma-current direction.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which energy is transferred to or from the counter-passing orbit population per unit physical volume. It is the orbit-class specialization of power density; counter-passing particles are passing particles that circulate opposite to the plasma-current direction, distinct from [co-passing power density](name:co_passing_power_density) and [trapped power density](name:trapped_power_density).

For the underlying local energy balance, volumetric power density is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{cp}} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{cp}}}{dt\,dV}
$$

where $E_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the energy transferred to the counter-passing population, $t$ is time, and $V$ is physical volume. The flux-surface average is applied to this local rate while retaining its per-volume meaning.

Positive values denote net energy gain by the counter-passing population; negative values denote net energy loss. Wave-particle interactions, collisions, and particle sources contribute when they are included in the counter-passing energy balance.

items.name: parallel_gyrocenter_momentum_flux_normalized_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description: Normalized parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular-momentum flux of a gyrokinetic eigenmode due to E×B drift is the rotating-frame spectral contribution from the perturbed electrostatic potential’s E×B drift to the mode’s parallel gyrocenter momentum transport.
items.documentation:
Normalized parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular-momentum flux of a gyrokinetic eigenmode due to $E\times B$ drift is the normalized spectral contribution, evaluated in the rotating frame, of the perturbed electrostatic potential's $E\times B$ drift to the parallel gyrocenter part of toroidal angular-momentum flux. The toroidal component is the $\hat{\phi}$ component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The normalization is defined relative to the reference momentum-flux normalization for the same eigenmode:

$$
\widehat{\Pi}_{\parallel,\phi}^{E\times B} = \frac{\Pi_{\parallel,\phi}^{E\times B}}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $\widehat{\Pi}_{\parallel,\phi}^{E\times B}$ is this normalized contribution, $\Pi_{\parallel,\phi}^{E\times B}$ is the corresponding unnormalized parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular-momentum-flux contribution from the perturbed electrostatic-potential $E\times B$ drift in the rotating frame, $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference momentum-flux normalization, $E$ is the perturbed electric field associated with the electrostatic potential, $B$ is the magnetic field, the subscript $\parallel$ denotes the part associated with gyrocenter motion parallel to $B$, and the subscript $\phi$ denotes toroidal angular momentum about the symmetry axis.

The quantity applies to one specified linear gyrokinetic eigenmode and to the rotating-frame representation of that mode; it is not summed over eigenmodes, wave-number spectrum, or transport channels. Its aggregation convention is a single-channel normalized eigenmode contribution, not a total turbulent momentum flux.

It is the electrostatic-potential $E\times B$ channel in the additive decomposition of the normalized parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular-momentum flux. The perturbed parallel vector-potential channel and the [perturbed parallel magnetic-field channel](name:parallel_gyrocenter_momentum_flux_normalized_of_gyrokinetic_eigenmode_due_to_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field) are separate contributions and are excluded from this quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when the $E\times B$-drift contribution transports positive parallel gyrocenter toroidal angular momentum across a magnetic flux surface toward increasing flux label, with positive toroidal angular momentum corresponding to the $+\hat{\phi}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: volume_averaged_neutral_temperature
items.description: Volume-averaged neutral temperature is the translational kinetic temperature, expressed as energy per particle, of a neutral population throughout the plasma volume inside the last closed magnetic flux surface during plasma initiation.
items.documentation:
Volume-averaged neutral temperature is the translational kinetic temperature of a neutral population during plasma initiation, representing random translational energy after removal of mean flow. It excludes energy stored in internal excitation or other internal quantum states.

The volume average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_{n} = \frac{1}{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}}\int_{V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}} T_n(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\overline{T}_{n}$ is the volume-averaged neutral temperature, $T_n(\mathbf{x})$ is the local translational kinetic temperature of the neutral population at position $\mathbf{x}$, $V_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is the plasma volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the differential physical-volume element.

The quantity applies to the represented neutral population throughout the volume enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface during plasma initiation. Its aggregation convention is an arithmetic spatial volume average of the local temperature, not a local value or a density-weighted particle average. It does not select only the cold or energetic neutral component and is not restricted to a particular internal quantum state.

This quantity is obtained by applying the volume-averaging transformation to [neutral temperature](name:neutral_temperature), with the local population and state aggregation inherited from that quantity. [Cold neutral temperature](name:cold_neutral_temperature) and [hot neutral temperature](name:hot_neutral_temperature_at_plasma_boundary) are population-restricted alternatives, while [neutral internal state temperature](name:neutral_internal_state_temperature) resolves a specified internal state rather than the generic neutral population.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity
items.description: Major-radius projection of the mean flow of ions of one specified species and ionization charge state, directed toward or away from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
The radial ion charge-state velocity is the projection of the bulk [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity) onto the direction of increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It describes mean translational motion within one specified ion species and ionization charge state.

The component is defined by the projected first velocity moment:

$$
u_{R,q}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\mathbf R}\cdot\mathbf u_q(\mathbf r)=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf R})f_q(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_q(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}
$$

where $u_{R,q}$ is the radial bulk velocity, $\mathbf u_q$ is the charge-state bulk velocity vector, $q$ is the ionic charge number, $\mathbf r$ is position, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $f_q$ is the velocity distribution of the selected species and charge state. The integration covers particle velocity space. Here $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical position, and $\hat{\mathbf R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing $R$.

The component is evaluated at the position of maximum major radius on each magnetic flux surface; it is not a flux-surface average. It retains charge-state resolution rather than combining charge states. The corresponding [radial ion velocity](name:radial_ion_velocity) is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of the species, not their sum.

This signed component is distinct from flow speed, random thermal motion, and particle flux. The major-radius direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface, so this quantity is not a flux-surface-normal velocity.

Sign convention: Positive when the charge-state bulk flow projects toward increasing major radius, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: radial_total_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective radial velocity coefficient for advective, non-diffusive transport of total plasma momentum in the edge plasma, distinct from the plasma bulk flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient describing the radial advective, non-diffusive transport of total plasma momentum in the edge plasma. It is a transport closure quantity, not an actual plasma bulk flow velocity.

For the selected total-momentum component, the radial convective flux is defined by

$$
\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}} = V_{\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}} P_\mathrm{tot}
$$

where $\Gamma_{P_\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective flux of total plasma momentum, $V_{\mathrm{tot},r,\mathrm{conv}}$ is this radial total-momentum convection velocity, and $P_\mathrm{tot}$ is the corresponding total plasma momentum density. The relation applies componentwise when the transported momentum component is resolved.

The scope is total plasma momentum in the edge plasma, aggregated according to the total-momentum transport equation and evaluated for radial transport. It excludes species-resolved, charge-state-resolved, neutral-only, and separately attributed momentum-convection contributions, and it must not be interpreted as the plasma bulk flow velocity. As a radial specialization of the [total momentum convection velocity](name:total_momentum_convection_velocity), it fixes the transport direction to the outward radial direction; it differs from the [radial neutral particle convection velocity](name:radial_neutral_particle_convection_velocity), which describes neutral-particle transport rather than total plasma momentum transport.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective total-momentum flux is directed toward increasing major-radius coordinate $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame for positive transported total-momentum density.

items.name: radius_of_passive_loop
items.description: Radius of the annular cross-section of a passive conducting loop element is the Euclidean distance from the cross-section center to a specified conducting boundary. It is nonnegative and does not denote the loop center's major-radius position.
items.documentation:
Radius of the annular cross-section of a passive conducting loop element is the Euclidean distance, in the $(R,Z)$ plane at fixed toroidal angle $phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, phi, Z)$ frame, from the center of the annular conductor cross-section to a specified conducting boundary of that annulus. Here $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The boundary radius is defined by the poloidal-plane distance from the cross-section center to the selected boundary point:

$$
r = \sqrt{(R_b - R_c)^2 + (Z_b - Z_c)^2}
$$

where $(R_c,Z_c)$ is the center position of the annular cross-section and $(R_b,Z_b)$ is the selected boundary position in the same fixed-$phi$ plane; all coordinate components in the equation are expressed in meters.

This parent quantity abstracts over [inner_radius_of_passive_loop](name:inner_radius_of_passive_loop) and [outer_radius_of_passive_loop](name:outer_radius_of_passive_loop). It satisfies $r \ge 0$ and is a size of the conductor cross-section, not a signed component along $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, or $\hat{Z}$ and not the major-radius coordinate of the loop center. For a circular annulus, [area_of_passive_loop](name:area_of_passive_loop) is related by $A=\pi(r_\mathrm{outer}^2-r_\mathrm{inner}^2)$, and thickness_of_passive_loop is $r_\mathrm{outer}-r_\mathrm{inner}$.

items.name: plasma_electrical_conductivity
items.description: Local plasma electrical-conductivity tensor mapping the electric-field vector to the conductive current-density vector, including anisotropic diagonal and off-diagonal coupling.
items.documentation:
Plasma electrical conductivity is the local rank-two material response that relates the plasma electric field to the conductive electric-current density. It represents the collective plasma response without selecting a particular species, orbit class, direction, or transport mechanism.

$$
\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}} = \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\mathrm{plasma}} \cdot \mathbf{E}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the conductive electric-current-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma electrical-conductivity tensor, and $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector. In components, $J_i = \sigma_{ij}E_j$, where $i$ identifies the current-density direction and $j$ identifies the electric-field direction. The tensor may be represented in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, or in the magnetic-field-aligned basis $(\hat{b},\hat{e}_{\perp 1},\hat{e}_{\perp 2})$, where $\hat{b}$ is the local magnetic-field direction.

The full tensor retains all diagonal and off-diagonal couplings and is therefore broader than any single component coefficient. It excludes displacement current and contributions that are not the local conductive response of the plasma. The [radial conductivity](name:radial_conductivity), [toroidal conductivity](name:toroidal_conductivity), and [vertical conductivity](name:vertical_conductivity) are diagonal component instances in the cylindrical frame; [poloidal conductivity](name:poloidal_conductivity) and [parallel conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity) are corresponding projections in flux-surface-tangent and magnetic-field-aligned directions, respectively.

items.name: radial_ion_particle_convection_velocity
items.description: Radial component of the effective convective velocity used for ion particle transport in the edge plasma, taken along increasing major radius R in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It represents collective particle-transport advection and is distinct from the ion fluid velocity.
items.documentation:
Radial component of the effective convective velocity used for ion particle transport is the scalar transport velocity whose multiplication by ion particle density gives the advective part of the ion particle flux in the radial direction. For this quantity, the radial direction is the major-radius direction $\hat R$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The defining relation for the radial convective contribution to the ion particle flux is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = n_i v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective ion particle flux, $n_i$ is the ion particle density, and $v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial ion particle convection velocity.

The quantity applies to collective ion particle transport in the edge plasma and to the ion species as a whole. Because velocity is an intensive per-particle field, the species-level ion value is the density-weighted mean over all ion charge states; if $q$ indexes ion charge state, $v_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convection velocity of charge state $q$, and $n_{i,q}$ is its particle density, then $v_{i,R}^{\mathrm{conv}} = (\sum_q n_{i,q} v_{i,q,R}^{\mathrm{conv}})/(\sum_q n_{i,q})$.

This is an effective transport coefficient, not the ion fluid velocity, not an individual charge-state flow velocity, and not the diffusive contribution to the radial particle flux. A flux-surface-normal convection velocity is a different projection; it coincides with this radial component only where the flux-surface normal is parallel to $\hat R$.

The direction-complement and population-resolved sibling [parallel ion charge-state convection velocity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_convection_velocity) describes the magnetic-field-parallel convective velocity for one ion charge state. This quantity instead describes the radial component for the charge-state-aggregated ion population.

Sign convention: Positive when the velocity is directed toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: co_passing_torque_density
items.description: Net angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume for the co-passing plasma population, retaining the complete torque-vector direction and all applicable transfer mechanisms.
items.documentation:
Torque density for the co-passing plasma population is the net angular-momentum transfer rate to that population per unit volume. It retains the complete torque-vector direction rather than selecting a toroidal component or a particular transfer mechanism.

The defining relation is

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{1}{\Delta V}\frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{co}}}{dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the angular momentum of the co-passing population, $\Delta V$ is a volume element, and $t$ is time.

Unless a mechanism qualifier is present, the quantity is the net sum of all applicable angular-momentum transfer contributions. The [toroidal co-passing torque density](name:toroidal_co_passing_torque_density) is its major-radius-weighted toroidal projection, while [toroidal torque density](name:toroidal_torque_density) selects the corresponding toroidal component without restricting the orbit class. The [torque density](name:torque_density) parent provides the common vector quantity.

Sign convention: Positive when each resolved component points along the corresponding positive unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ basis, with $\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$.

items.name: width_of_iron_core_segment
items.description: Full non-negative radial extent of an iron core segment’s rectangular cross-section, measured along major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The iron core segment width is the complete radial span between the inner and outer faces of its rectangular cross-section. It is a geometric extent, not the radial position of the segment or the curvature radius of an arc boundary.

The width is defined by

$$
w_{\rm iron} = R_{\rm outer} - R_{\rm inner}
$$

where $R_{\rm outer}$ and $R_{\rm inner}$ are the major-radius coordinates in meters of the outer and inner radial faces, respectively, and $w_{\rm iron}$ is the resulting full extent. The width complements the [height of the iron core segment](name:height_of_iron_core_segment), while the [outer radius of the iron core segment](name:outer_radius_of_iron_core_segment) identifies a boundary position rather than a cross-sectional span.

items.name: fast_particle_density
items.description: Local or flux-surface-averaged concentration of suprathermal particles of a selected species, including trapped and passing orbits and excluding thermal particles.
items.documentation:
Fast-particle number density is the concentration of the suprathermal, nonthermal population of a selected species. It includes all orbit classes and may denote either a local density or its magnetic-flux-surface average.

The local density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the fast-particle distribution:

$$
n_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\int f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-particle number density, $s$ labels the selected species, $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is its fast-particle velocity distribution, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $t$ is time, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The flux-surface-averaged form is the differential-volume-weighted average of this local moment over a magnetic flux surface. Superposed fast populations of the same species contribute additively; different species are not implicitly combined. For an ion species specified without charge-state resolution, the fast-particle density is summed over all charge states.

This quantity is the fast-population contribution to [particle density](name:particle_density), which also includes thermal particles. The thermal population is excluded here; the name does not prescribe a universal energy threshold separating the populations.

Orbit restrictions define [co-passing fast-particle density](name:co_passing_fast_particle_density), [counter-passing fast-particle density](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_density), and [trapped fast-particle density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density). For a complete, nonoverlapping orbit partition, these contributions sum to the fast-particle density when evaluated with the same species selection and averaging convention. Volume integration, followed by summation over the included species, gives the [total fast-particle count](name:total_fast_particle_count).

items.name: vertical_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description: Vertical (Z) component of the vacuum magnetic vector potential produced solely by toroidal-field coil currents in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical component $A_Z$ of the vacuum magnetic vector potential is the projection of $\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ onto the vertical direction $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It represents the $Z$-directed contribution of the vector field generated exclusively by toroidal-field coil currents in the absence of plasma and eddy-current contributions, forming part of the complete [vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) vector $(A_R, A_\phi, A_Z)$.

The vacuum magnetic field is related to the vector potential by

$$
\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}
$$

where $\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the vacuum magnetic field, $\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ is the vacuum magnetic vector potential, and $\nabla \times$ is the curl operator. The curl is gage-invariant, whereas $A_Z$ depends on the selected gage and is not itself a magnetic-field component. The complementary radial component is [radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential](name:radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential); unlike [vertical_magnetic_vector_potential](name:vertical_magnetic_vector_potential), this quantity excludes plasma and eddy-current contributions.

Sign convention: Positive when $A_Z$ points in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description: Radial (R) component of the vacuum magnetic vector potential produced solely by toroidal-field coil currents in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial component $A_R$ of the vacuum magnetic vector potential is the projection of $\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ onto the radial direction $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It represents the $R$-directed component of the gage-dependent vector potential produced solely by toroidal-field coil currents.

The component projection is defined by:

$$
A_R = \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the [vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential), $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\cdot$ denotes the scalar product.

The source population is the toroidal-field coil current system only. Contributions from plasma currents and from other external-current systems are excluded; the quantity is a pointwise scalar component, not a spatial average, flux-surface average, integral, magnetic-induction component, or the full [magnetic vector potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential).

The corresponding vacuum magnetic induction $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is related to the parent vector by $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}} = \nabla \times \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$, with $\nabla \times$ denoting the curl operator. Replacing $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ by $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}} + \nabla \chi$, where $\chi$ is an arbitrary scalar gage function, changes $A_R$ by the radial projection of $\nabla \chi$ while leaving $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ unchanged; the [vertical vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:vertical_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) is the analogous projection along $\hat{Z}$, the vertical basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ has a projection along $+\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states and excluding neutral nitrogen.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the nitrogen ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local nitrogen-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all nitrogen ionic charge states. It represents nitrogen ions specifically, rather than neutral nitrogen, electrons, or other ion species.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{N,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{N,ion}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{N,axis}}$ is the nitrogen-ion number density at the magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{N,ion}}$ is the total number of nitrogen ions summed over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the complete nitrogen-ion population at that location, uses a sum over nitrogen ionic charge states, and excludes neutral nitrogen; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of another species.

This is the nitrogen-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It follows the same charge-state-summed convention as [helium-4 density at the magnetic axis](name:helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis), while differing in the ion species counted.

items.name: width_of_passive_structure
items.description: Full radial extent of a rectangular passive conducting structure element in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial width is the full major-radius extent of a rectangular passive conducting structure element, measured between its inner and outer radial boundaries.

$$
W = R_{\mathrm{outer}} - R_{\mathrm{inner}}
$$

where $W$ is the radial width, and $R_{\mathrm{outer}}$ and $R_{\mathrm{inner}}$ are the major-radius coordinates in meters of the outer and inner boundaries in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The quantity is non-negative and describes radial extent only; it is distinct from the full vertical extent given by [height of passive structure](name:height_of_passive_structure) and from the element length given by length of passive structure.

items.name: torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Local rate at which collisions transfer angular momentum to or from a plasma population, expressed as torque per unit volume.
items.documentation:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate imparted to a specified plasma population by collisional interactions, divided by volume. It applies to electron, ion, charge-state, and orbit-class populations, including the specific cases represented by [electron collisional torque density](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [ion collisional torque density](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

For a resolved scalar torque component, the defining relation is

$$
\tau_{s,\mathrm{coll}} = \left.\frac{\partial \ell_s}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{s,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque density, $\ell_s$ is the corresponding angular-momentum density of population $s$, and the subscript indicates that only collisional transfer is included.

The quantity excludes torque caused by electromagnetic forces, pressure forces, or other noncollisional processes. More specific population and orbit restrictions, such as co-passing fast-ion charge-state collisional torque density, refine the recipient population without changing the underlying definition.

Sign convention: Positive when collisions increase the resolved angular momentum of the recipient population.

items.name: outer_radius_of_iron_core_segment
items.description: Radius of an iron-core segment is the non-negative geometry radius used to define its outer boundary in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame about the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Radius of an iron-core segment is the non-negative geometry radius that defines the outer boundary of an annular iron-core region. This member specializes radius of an iron-core segment to the outermost boundary measured from the toroidal symmetry axis. The relevant cross-section is the plane spanned by $R$ and $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height.

The outer radius is the maximum major-radius coordinate on the cross-sectional boundary:

$$
r_{\rm out} = \max_{(R,Z)\in\partial A} R
$$

where $r_{\rm out}$ is the outer radius, $A$ is the iron-core cross-sectional region, and $\partial A$ is its boundary; $R$, $Z$, and $r_{\rm out}$ are expressed in meters.

For annular geometry, the outer radius together with the [inner radius of an iron-core segment](name:inner_radius_of_iron_core_segment) determines the radial thickness through $r_{\rm out}-r_{\rm in}$. It is an axis-referenced outer extent, not the radius of a local circular arc about an explicit off-axis center or the full rectangular extent described by the [width of an iron-core segment](name:width_of_iron_core_segment).

items.name: ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming bound component-by-component, capping flux magnitude while preserving its sign.
items.documentation:
The ion momentum coefficient is a dimensionless flux-limiter parameter for gradient-driven momentum transport, providing one limiter factor for each selected spatial transport component. It is the ion specialization of [momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), scaling the collisionless free-streaming bound while preserving the direction supplied by the underlying diffusive closure.

For each selected component, the limited momentum-flux density is defined by the harmonic-mean closure:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}}
$$

where $\alpha_m$ is the momentum-flux limiter coefficient, $\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the collisionless free-streaming reference momentum-flux density, $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux estimate, and $\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the resulting limited flux density.

The shared quantity spans parallel, poloidal, and radial ion components; [parallel ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:parallel_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) and [poloidal ion momentum-flux limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) are concrete instances. It applies to momentum flux rather than particle, heat, or energy flux, and the coefficient is non-negative.

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part
items.description: Toroidal perturbed plasma velocity real part is the real part of the complex amplitude of the toroidal component of the first-order plasma velocity perturbation for a single toroidal Fourier harmonic with mode number n in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the in-phase eigenfunction component relative to the chosen complex phase, not the equilibrium toroidal flow.
items.documentation:
Toroidal perturbed plasma velocity real part is the real part of the complex amplitude of the toroidal component of the first-order plasma velocity perturbation for a single toroidal Fourier harmonic with mode number $n$. The toroidal component is the projection along $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$, the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. It represents the in-phase part of the linear magnetohydrodynamic perturbation eigenfunction relative to the chosen complex phase, not the equilibrium toroidal flow.

The component is defined by projecting the complex velocity eigenfunction for the selected harmonic onto the toroidal basis direction and taking the real part:

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Re},n}(R,Z) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\widetilde{\mathbf v}_n(R,Z)\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}\right]
$$

where $v_{\phi,\mathrm{Re},n}$ is this quantity, $\widetilde{\mathbf v}_n$ is the complex first-order plasma velocity eigenfunction for toroidal mode number $n$, $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the toroidal unit vector, and $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes the real part. With toroidal dependence proportional to $\exp(i n\phi)$, $i$ is the imaginary unit.

Together with [toroidal perturbed plasma velocity imaginary part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part), this quantity forms the complex toroidal perturbed velocity amplitude. Because a linear eigenfunction may be multiplied by an arbitrary complex constant, the division into real and imaginary parts depends on the selected normalization and phase; the quadrature component is the linked imaginary part, not a separate physical velocity direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the real toroidal velocity component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: area_of_passive_loop
items.description: Area of a passive loop is the non-negative cross-sectional area of conducting material in a passive loop element, taken on a section normal to the local current path. It excludes the aperture enclosed by the loop.
items.documentation:
Area of a passive loop is the non-negative cross-sectional area of the solid conducting material of a passive conducting loop element, evaluated on a surface normal to the local current path. It is a material cross-section of the conductor, not the aperture enclosed by the loop or the area swept out by the loop centerline.

The general geometric definition is the area of the conducting region $\mathcal{S}$ in that normal cross-section:

$$
A = \int_{\mathcal{S}} dS
$$

where $A$ is the passive-loop conductor area, $\mathcal{S}$ is the subset of the section occupied by conducting material, and $dS$ is the scalar surface-area element.

For an annular cross-section, this definition gives $A = \pi(r_o^2-r_i^2)$, where $r_i$ and $r_o$ are the [inner](name:inner_radius_of_passive_loop) and [outer](name:outer_radius_of_passive_loop) radii measured from the annulus center to the conducting boundaries. For a non-annular cross-section, $\mathcal{S}$ is the bounded conducting region defined by the conductor geometry; parameters such as thickness, width, or height describe that boundary but are not themselves the area.

items.name: electron_source_rate_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection
items.description: Electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection is the charge-weighted electron-equivalent production rate from ablation and ionization of pellet material at a specified position along the injected pellet trajectory.
items.documentation:
Electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection is the charge-weighted electron-equivalent production rate from ablation and ionization of pellet material at a specified position along the injected pellet trajectory. It counts the free-electron source associated with material reaching that path position, not the electron concentration of the surrounding plasma.

For trajectory coordinate $\ell$ and time $t$, the local rate is defined by the charge-weighted sum over ablated pellet constituents contributing at that same path position:

$$
S_e(\ell,t) = \sum_a Z_a^\mathrm{eff}(\ell,t)\,\dot{N}_a(\ell,t)
$$

where $S_e$ is the electron source rate at the pellet path due to pellet injection, $a$ indexes the pellet constituents or represented charge-state groups, $\dot{N}_a$ is the local production rate of constituent $a$ by ablation and ionization, and $Z_a^\mathrm{eff}$ is the effective number of free electrons contributed by one produced constituent. For a fully ionized atomic constituent, $Z_a^\mathrm{eff}$ reduces to its nuclear charge.

This is a path-position rate, not a source density per distance along the pellet trajectory or a volume-integrated source. The [electron source rate due to injection](name:electron_source_rate_due_to_injection) is obtained only after aggregating the appropriate local electron-equivalent contributions, while electron density of pellet path describes electron concentration along the same trajectory. The [accumulated particle count at pellet path due to pellet injection](name:accumulated_particle_count_at_pellet_path_due_to_pellet_injection) is an unweighted cumulative particle count; it is not an electron-equivalent accumulated source unless the same charge weighting and time integration are applied.

The value is non-negative and is zero where injected pellet material at the considered path position does not produce free electrons.

items.name: brightness_of_visible_camera
items.description: Visible-camera brightness is band-integrated photon radiance along a specified viewing direction over the wavelengths admitted by a visible passband. It gives the photon rate per projected collecting area and accepted solid angle, with the spectral dependence integrated over that band.
items.documentation:
Visible-camera brightness is the photon radiance of a radiation field along a specified viewing direction after integration over a visible wavelength interval or passband. It is normalized to projected collecting area, observation time, and accepted solid angle, and counts photons rather than radiant energy.

The band-integrated photon radiance is defined by integrating the spectral photon radiance over the visible passband:

$$
B_\mathrm{vis} = \int_{\lambda_1}^{\lambda_2} L_\lambda^{(\gamma)}(\lambda)\, d\lambda
$$

where $B_\mathrm{vis}$ is the visible-camera brightness, $L_\lambda^{(\gamma)}(\lambda)$ is the spectral photon radiance at wavelength $\lambda$, and $[\lambda_1,\lambda_2]$ is the wavelength interval defining the visible passband.

The quantity is non-negative because spectral photon radiance is non-negative over the passband. It is distinct from spectral radiance, which retains wavelength dependence, and from [radiance at spectral line](name:photon_radiance_at_spectral_line), which refers to an individual spectral line or narrow line interval; it also differs from energy radiance because photons are counted without weighting by photon energy.

items.name: krypton_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron krypton source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected krypton atom with Z = 36 contributes 36 equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation:
The krypton source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral krypton with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. Each neutral krypton atom contributes $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ equivalent electrons to the equivalent particle inventory; this accounting uses nuclear charge and does not imply ionization at the injection location.

The defining relation for krypton injection is:

$$
\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}
$$

where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton equivalent-electron source rate in equivalent-electron counts per second, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the neutral krypton atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} = 36$ is the atomic number of krypton.

This is the krypton-species contribution to [source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) and is the instantaneous time derivative of [accumulated_krypton_count](name:accumulated_krypton_count) when the same equivalent-electron accounting is used. It excludes krypton supplied by mechanisms other than gas injection and differs from gas_particle_source_rate_over_vessel_due_to_gas_injection, which is counted as raw gas-phase particles rather than equivalent electrons. It is directly parallel to same-family species quantities such as [argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), differing by the injected species and its atomic number.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_flux_surface
items.description: Major-radius coordinate of a flux surface, defined as the midpoint between its minimum and maximum major-radius values in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of flux surface

In the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ basis, with coordinate values $(R,\phi,Z)$, the surface coordinate is defined as the midpoint of those extrema:

$$
R_{\mathrm{fs}} = \frac{R_{\min} + R_{\max}}{2}
$$

where $R_{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the representative major-radius coordinate assigned to the flux surface, $R_{\min}$ and $R_{\max}$ are the minimum and maximum values, respectively, of $R$ over that complete surface, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The extrema are taken over the complete flux surface, and their midpoint is the aggregation convention; this quantity is not an area-, volume-, or flux-weighted average. It is a single surface-level value, not a pointwise coordinate or the sequence of coordinates along the [radial outline of a flux surface](name:radial_outline_of_flux_surface).

This quantity specializes the [major-radius coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) to a flux surface by representing the surface’s full range with one extrema midpoint. It differs from the [normalized minor radius of a flux surface](name:normalized_minor_radius_of_flux_surface), which expresses radial position as a normalized quantity.

A surface formed by points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a nested-flux-surface configuration. Where $\psi(R, Z) = \mathrm{const}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux.

items.name: neutron_flux_at_first_wall
items.description: Neutron-carried energy flux arriving at the plasma-facing first-wall surface, providing the carrier-specific local contribution to energy delivered from the plasma to first-wall material.
items.documentation:
Neutron energy flux at the plasma-facing first-wall surface is the local rate of neutron-carried energy delivered per unit surface area. It is the neutron-specific contribution to the energy flux associated with plasma loading of the first wall.

$$
q_n(\mathbf{x}) = \int_0^\infty E\,\Phi_n(E,\mathbf{x})\,dE
$$

where $q_n(\mathbf{x})$ is the local neutron energy flux, $\mathbf{x}$ is a position on the first-wall surface, $E$ is neutron energy, and $\Phi_n(E,\mathbf{x})$ is the differential neutron number flux at that position and energy.

This quantity is local on the first-wall surface, integrates over neutron energy, and includes only the neutron carrier. It is not integrated over the surface and does not include photon, charged-particle, or other plasma-wall energy carriers. It describes energy arriving at the surface rather than nuclear energy deposited throughout the wall volume, which is represented by [nuclear power density of breeder blanket layer](name:nuclear_power_density_of_breeder_blanket_layer).

The quantity contributes to the total local energy flux represented by [flux_at_first_wall](name:flux_at_first_wall). The representative [neutron_flux_maximum_at_first_wall](name:neutron_flux_maximum_at_first_wall) is obtained by taking the maximum of $q_n(\mathbf{x})$ over the relevant first-wall surface, while this parent quantity remains the local carrier-specific flux.

items.name: fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions
items.description: Fast-particle power due to collisions is the volume-integrated Coulomb collisional power transferred from the fast, non-Maxwellian particle population to the bulk electron population.
items.documentation:
Fast-particle power due to collisions is the net rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from the fast, non-Maxwellian particle population to the bulk electron population. It is the plasma-volume integral of the local collisional energy-transfer density for this donor-recipient population pair.

The volume-integrated transfer is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast}\to e}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{fast}\to e}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})\, dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast}\to e}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-particle power due to collisions, $p_{\mathrm{fast}\to e}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local Coulomb collisional energy-transfer density from the fast-particle population to the bulk electron population, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is the differential volume element.

The quantity applies to all fast particles belonging to the non-Maxwellian population in the plasma, including all orbit classes and any unresolved subdivisions such as source, energy, pitch, species, or charge-state groups. Its aggregation convention is a sum over all included fast-particle subpopulations and over the plasma volume.

It excludes collisional power transferred from fast particles to bulk ion populations, collisional exchange internal to the bulk thermal populations, non-collisional heating, field or wave power, launched or generator power, and power retained in or lost with fast particles rather than deposited in bulk electrons.

This quantity is the fast-particle donor component of [thermal electron power due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions) when that electron power is decomposed by source population. Summing analogous recipient-species components gives the total Coulomb collisional energy loss of the fast-particle population.

Sign convention: Positive when net Coulomb collisional energy transfer is from the fast-particle population to the bulk electron population.

items.name: thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure
items.description: Pressure of thermal neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or excitation state, arising from random translational motion rather than bulk flow or suprathermal particles.
items.documentation:
Pressure of thermal neutral particles of one species in a specified internal quantum or excitation state is the isotropic mechanical stress from their random translational motion. It is the thermal-population component of [neutral internal-state pressure](name:neutral_internal_state_pressure).

The pressure is defined by the central second velocity moment of the thermal distribution:

$$
p_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}} = \frac{m_0}{3}\int |\mathbf{c}|^2 f_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{c})\,d^3c
$$

where $p_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the state-resolved thermal neutral pressure, $m_0$ is the particle mass of the selected neutral species, $a$ labels its internal state, $\mathbf{c}$ is particle velocity relative to the thermal population's mean flow, $f_{0,a}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is its number-density distribution in that relative velocity, and $d^3c$ is the velocity-space volume element. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, and the superscript $\mathrm{th}$ denotes the thermal population.

The quantity applies to the Maxwellian thermal population in one internal state, with no sum over internal states or species. In the edge and scrape-off-layer setting, it is evaluated locally at the outboard equatorial midplane rather than averaged over a flux surface. It is the state-resolved counterpart of [thermal neutral pressure](name:thermal_neutral_pressure).

Bulk-flow momentum flux and internal excitation energy are excluded: the internal state selects the particles but does not contribute excitation energy to their translational pressure. Unlike [total neutral internal-state pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure), this quantity excludes the nonthermal contribution described by [suprathermal neutral internal-state pressure](name:suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure).

items.name: minimum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Lower allowable value of a signed electromagnetic force resultant for poloidal-field coils, with its magnitude and sign defined by one row of the force-combination matrix.
items.documentation:
Minimum force of a poloidal-field coil is the lower allowable value of a signed electromagnetic force resultant acting on the poloidal-field coil system. Each row of the force-combination matrix defines one resultant by weighting the radial and vertical components of the [force of a poloidal-field coil](name:force_of_poloidal_field_coil).

For combination row $k$, the resultant is defined by

$$
F_{\mathrm{comb},k}=w_{kR}F_R+w_{kZ}F_Z
$$

where $F_R$ and $F_Z$ are the radial and vertical electromagnetic-force components, $w_{kR}$ and $w_{kZ}$ are the row weights, and $k$ identifies the combination row. The minimum value satisfies $F_{\min,k}\leq F_{\mathrm{comb},k}$ for the applicable row. Unlike the [maximum force of a poloidal-field coil](name:maximum_force_of_poloidal_field_coil), this quantity specifies the lower structural bound rather than the upper bound.

Sign convention: Positive when the vertical force component is directed upward along $+Z$ and the radial force component is directed outward along increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description: Characteristic outward distance over which a decaying plasma quantity decreases by one e-folding in the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the e-folding distance for a plasma quantity that decreases outward from the confined plasma into the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The operand may be a particle density, temperature, or heat-flux magnitude.

$$
L_f = \left|\frac{d\ln f}{dx}\right|^{-1}
$$

where $L_f$ is the e-folding length, $f$ is the positive scalar quantity or magnitude being characterized, and $x$ is outward distance from the confined plasma in the direction normal to magnetic flux surfaces. The scale is defined locally where the logarithmic gradient is nonzero.

The general quantity includes the electron number-density specialization [electron decay length](name:electron_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer), the ion number-density specialization ion decay length, and the heat-flux specialization [heat decay length](name:heat_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer). It does not select a species, transport channel, or particular decaying quantity.

items.name: width_of_ferritic_element
items.description: Full non-negative radial extent of a ferritic element’s rectangular cross-section, measured along major radius in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the full non-negative radial extent of a ferritic element’s rectangular cross-section, measured along the major-radius direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It spans the inner and outer radial boundaries of the cross-section.

$$
w_R = R_{\mathrm{out}} - R_{\mathrm{in}}
$$

where $w_R$ is the radial extent, and $R_{\mathrm{out}}$ and $R_{\mathrm{in}}$ are the outer and inner major-radius coordinates, respectively, measured in meters.

This is a geometric width, not the radial coordinate of the [ferritic element centroid](name:radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid), the outer boundary radius of an annular representation, or the extent in the vertical direction. It is analogous to the [width of an iron core segment](name:width_of_iron_core_segment).

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description: Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified thermal ion charge state within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified thermal ion charge state within the plasma volume enclosed by a specified magnetic flux surface. It is the portion of wave power transferred to thermal ions in that charge state, accumulated over the volume inside the chosen surface.

The cumulative power is defined by integrating the local absorbed-wave-power density for that thermal ion charge state over the enclosed plasma volume:

$$
P_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\lambda) = \int_{V(\lambda)} p_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{x}) \, dV
$$

where $P_q^{\mathrm{th}}(\lambda)$ is the cumulative absorbed wave power for thermal ion charge state $q$ inside the magnetic flux surface labeled by $\lambda$, $p_q^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the local absorbed-wave-power density for that thermal ion charge state, and $V(\lambda)$ is the plasma volume enclosed by that magnetic flux surface.

This quantity is charge-state resolved and includes only absorption by the thermal ion population; it excludes absorption by electrons, fast or non-thermal ions, neutrals, and non-wave power exchange. Because power is extensive, the sum over all thermal-ion charge states gives [thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:thermal_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface). It is the thermal-population contribution to [ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface); the corresponding fast-ion contribution is [fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

items.name: voltage_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description: Electrical potential difference associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna, defined between the antenna conductor or feed and its reference conductor. It is the general antenna-voltage quantity; specialized names specify amplitude or another representation of the waveform.
items.documentation:
Electrical potential difference associated with an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna is the scalar electric potential of the specified antenna conductor or feed relative to its associated reference conductor or node. It represents the antenna voltage waveform before any child name specifies a particular reduction or representation of that waveform.

The signed antenna voltage is defined by the potential difference between the antenna node and its reference node:

$$
V_\mathrm{ant}(t) = \Phi_\mathrm{ant}(t) - \Phi_\mathrm{ref}(t)
$$

where $V_\mathrm{ant}(t)$ is the antenna voltage, $\Phi_\mathrm{ant}(t)$ is the electric potential of the specified antenna conductor or feed, $\Phi_\mathrm{ref}(t)$ is the electric potential of its associated reference conductor or node, and $t$ is time.

The scope is voltages intrinsic to ion-cyclotron-heating antenna hardware, including antenna conductors, straps, or feeds when they are the defined electrical node. The unqualified parent does not by itself specify an instantaneous value, phasor, peak amplitude, root-mean-square value, or any aggregation over antenna elements; those distinctions belong to qualified child names.

The [voltage amplitude of an ion-cyclotron-heating antenna](name:voltage_amplitude_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) is a specialized reduction of this antenna voltage waveform to its peak magnitude. This parent is distinct from antenna current, generator voltage not defined at the antenna node, and launched or absorbed radio-frequency power.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric potential of the specified antenna conductor or feed is greater than the electric potential of its associated reference conductor or node.

items.name: radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description: Radiated power associated with a single breeder blanket module, abstracting over plasma electromagnetic power incident on the module surface, the reflected portion, and the absorbed portion retained as a module heat load as distinct radiation energy-budget components.
items.documentation:
Radiated power of a breeder blanket module quantifies the rate at which plasma electromagnetic emission, chiefly bremsstrahlung continuum and atomic line radiation, is assigned to the module-level radiation channel. It is the umbrella scalar for the incident photon power crossing onto the module surface and the absorbed photon power retained after surface reflection, represented by [incident_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:incident_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module) and [absorbed_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_breeder_blanket_module).

The radiated-power component for a single module is defined by integrating the corresponding radiative surface energy flux over the module surface:

$$
P_{\mathrm{rad},c} = \int_{A_m} \Phi_{\mathrm{rad},c}\, dA,\qquad c \in \{\mathrm{inc},\mathrm{abs}\}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{rad},c}$ is the module-level radiated-power component in watts, $A_m$ is the module plasma-facing surface, $dA$ is a surface element, $\Phi_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident photon energy flux density onto that surface, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{abs}}$ is the retained photon energy flux density after reflection.

The incident and absorbed components are related by the surface-reflection balance $P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{abs}} = P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{inc}} - P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{ref}}$, equivalently $P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{abs}} = (1-\mathcal{R})P_{\mathrm{rad},\mathrm{inc}}$ for an effective reflectance $\mathcal{R}$. The parent quantity is not a sum of incident and absorbed terms; it identifies the module radiation channel, while the component qualifier identifies which surface-budget term is represented. Neutron surface loads, volumetric nuclear energy deposition, auxiliary heating, and thermal radiation emitted by the module itself are outside this radiated-power channel; the absorbed part contributes to thermal_power_of_breeder_blanket_module within [power_of_breeder_blanket_module](name:power_of_breeder_blanket_module).

items.name: toroidal_electron_velocity
items.description: Signed component of the local mean electron flow tangent to circles about the symmetry axis, describing toroidal electron transport in the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
The toroidal electron velocity is the signed projection of the local electron-fluid bulk flow onto the toroidal direction in the edge plasma. This direction is tangent to circles about the symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position.

The defining projection is:

$$
v_{e,\phi} = \mathbf{v}_e \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $v_{e,\phi}$ is the toroidal electron velocity, $\mathbf{v}_e$ is the local [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle.

The underlying electron-fluid velocity is the particle-number-weighted first moment of the local electron velocity distribution, rather than the center-of-mass velocity of all plasma species. The toroidal component is a local linear velocity, not an angular velocity, the full flow magnitude, or a measure of random thermal motion; no spatial averaging is implied.

The [radial electron velocity](name:radial_electron_velocity) projects the same electron-fluid velocity along increasing major radius, rather than around the symmetry axis.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal electron flow is directed toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: cold_neutral_velocity
items.description: Cold neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk flow of low-energy neutral atoms, identified from the Doppler shift of their emission.
items.documentation:
Cold neutral velocity is the line-of-sight component of the bulk drift vector of a cold neutral particle population. It represents convective neutral motion after averaging over particle velocities and over the contributing cold-neutral population states.

The component is defined from the parent [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) by

$$
v_{n,c,ell} = \mathbf{v}_{n,c} \cdot \hat{\ell}
$$
